Combined with the leading Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation, this gives the down-sector Cabibbo seed $\sqrt{m_d/m_s} = \sqrt{3/2} - 1 = 0.22474\ldots$, numerically close to the measured $|V_{us}| = 0.22503 \pm 0.00068$ ($0.4\sigma$). A full CKM evaluation requires the up-sector phase correction, which we defer. The correspondence is testable by future lattice QCD+QED determinations of $m_d/m_s$; explicit failure modes are listed.

papers.title: Soft normed linear spaces via soft elements: decomposition, convergence, and operators
papers.abstract: Let $F\colon A\to\mathcal{P}(X)$ be a soft linear subspace of a linear space $X$ over $\mathbb{K}$. Its soft elements form the product $\prod_{t\in A}F(t)$. We use this representation to characterize selection spaces, decompose soft norms and soft linear operators into their sectionwise parts, and compare soft, uniform, and componentwise convergence. We also characterize completeness and continuity in the box, extended-supremum, and product settings. Neumann-series and fixed-point results are obtained as applications.

papers.title: Taming Noise Initialization for Zero-shot Video Restoration with Image Diffusion Priors
papers.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in restoring high-quality images in a zero-shot manner. Unfortunately, extending this success to video restoration is challenging due to the substantial computational resources required to pre-train video diffusion models. A rising trend seeks to address video restoration by utilizing a pre-trained image diffusion model, initiating restoration from either frame-wise independent or identical Gaussian noise. Yet, these approaches often fall short, as such simple noise initiations fail to capture and utilize the inherent temporal correlations within degraded video frames. In this work, we propose taming noise initialization for zero-shot video restoration, which preserves the intrinsic temporal correlations by generating initial noises directly using DDIM inversion on the corrupted video frames themselves. Building on this, we introduce an adaptive noise blending strategy that suppresses degradation patterns encoded during DDIM inversion while gradually steering the noise toward a Gaussian distribution. To further emphasize temporal consistency, we propose measurement-guided trajectory attention to better align features across frames. Extensive experiments on multiple video restoration tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms existing zero-shot approaches, consistently achieving superior results on the DAVIS, REDS4, and Set8 datasets.

papers.title: Beyond QASecClaw: Agent Scaling, Verifier Feedback, and Evidence Reliability in Software Assurance
papers.abstract: Can additional specialist language-model contexts improve software assurance when deterministic tool evidence is already available? We study this question through five experiments spanning authored Java warning controls, OWASP Benchmark assessment, Defects4J test generation, SV-COMP assertion verdicts, and deliberately misleading evidence packages. The evaluated systems use Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, with a 1.5B sensitivity analysis, and complete 13,638 model requests. On eight related development warnings, increasing the context count from 1 to 50 increases token use 49-fold without improving unsafe clearance. On 160 OWASP cases, model configurations trade clearance against unresolved outcomes; the ten-context arm assesses only 96 cases. On 32 SV-COMP tasks, raw verifier feedback raises mean correct model verdicts from 12.7 to 22.0, but also raises incorrect verdicts from one to seven; a JBMC-plus-JVM validation baseline returns 26 correct verdicts and six unresolved outcomes. On two sets of 120 evidence packages, models reject 70-100% of applicable counterexamples, while construction-specific scope checks classify every package correctly. No target defect is discovered in three Defects4J bugs, one unsupported by the test adapter. These descriptive results support deterministic evidence admission for the tested settings, while exposing limits of verdict aggregation, feedback interpretation, and the available evaluation coverage.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts
papers.abstract: Automatic soccer event spotting supports highlight generation, video indexing, and sports analytics, but existing methods depend on large annotated datasets and soccer-specific training. We present a zero-shot framework that detects, classifies, and temporally localizes events in full-length soccer broadcasts without task-specific parameter training. Each match is segmented into overlapping clips represented by a compact visual storyboard and the aligned commentary transcript, which a general-purpose multimodal model processes jointly. On three manually annotated matches containing 130 events, the best configuration achieves 72.0% F1@5s and outperforms SoccerNet-trained CALF and NetVLAD++ in a cross-dataset setting, while the storyboard representation reduces inference cost by 72% compared with individual frames. We further analyze the effects of model family, input representation, and prompt optimization, and introduce an evidence-grounded excitement-scoring stage that ranks detected events with natural-language explanations for highlight selection.

authors.name: Mahmudul Hasan
authors.institution: Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: When Connectivity Misleads: Guiding Agentic Search with Contrastive Evidence Paths
papers.abstract: Search agents can use cross-document graphs to discover sources through multi-hop connections and choose subsequent actions based on candidate rankings and relationships within a limited observation window. However, documents may rank highly because their numerous connections make them easier to reach, without necessarily providing more valuable evidence. Graph diffusion methods such as Personalized PageRank (PPR) aggregate propagation contributions from multiple sources, allowing highly connected distractor nodes to crowd the observation window. Flat node scores also obscure cross-document evidence trails, limiting continued exploration. We propose Contrastive Evidence Paths (CEP), which scores candidates by their strongest individual paths on a query-conditioned document graph and calibrates these scores against the same graph's background visitation distribution to mitigate structural bias. CEP ranks candidates by the calibrated scores and retains the corresponding source paths. Building on CEP, we develop Structured Corpus Interaction (SCI), which organizes candidates and their connecting paths into a structured Map, enabling agents to verify source documents and pursue missing information through expansion from anchor documents. Experiments on BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-COVID show that SCI achieves state-of-the-art answer accuracy and nDCG@10 with the lowest generation cost. Compared with the strongest baselines by task performance, maximum reductions in tool calls and total generation costs exceed 50% and 40%, respectively. Further analysis confirms that SCI with CEP suppresses ranking inflation induced by structural connections and improves gold recall and exploration efficiency.

authors.name: Junhao Wen
authors.institution: State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Dynamical coarse-graining of neural-network training
papers.abstract: Dynamical coarse-graining of neural networks gives macroscopic observables and enables training to be predicted, and controlled in a state space far smaller than the parameter space. In this paper, we first define the learning operator following the training law of neural networks and establish a descent theorem for the learning operator, which serves to determine whether the operator is sufficient to characterize the learning dynamics. Then the exact closure theorem and the dynamic coarse-graining theorem are presented in sequence. The three theorems established in this paper provide a systematic framework for constructing and assessing dynamical coarse-grained models of neural-network training. Finally, we demonstrate the applicability of the theorems with a finite-width nonlinear ReLU network. Its dynamic coarse-grained model for a fixed pattern is exactly derived and composed of five independent moments. The model exactly predict the training outputs and evolving learning operator. The framework may also guide the development of approximate coarse-grained models for more general neural networks when exact closure is unavailable.

authors.name: Jianxiang Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: Fake news undermines public trust and the integrity of online information ecosystems. Temporally disordered fake news is especially elusive because it rearranges factual events into a false chronology. Individual events may remain factually valid even when their temporal relations are misrepresented. When similar events involving the same entity recur, retrieval may return semantically plausible evidence from the wrong period. Consequently, independent event verification may rely on locally coherent but temporally mismatched evidence and incorrectly validate the article. We call this the \textit{evidence coherence trap}. Because existing benchmarks rarely isolate this setting, we construct ChronoFake, a source-disjoint benchmark of 30,706 articles derived from temporally anchored real events. It distinguishes temporal manipulation from valid narration, including flashbacks. To address this, we propose DelSA, a \underline{D}ocument S\underline{el}ection \underline{S}elf-Updating \underline{A}gent that iteratively refines evidence selection during training and applies a frozen rulebook for one-pass evidence selection at inference. DelSA uses an LLM to characterize candidate evidence, while a verifier-trained reranker balances local relevance against timeline consistency. Finally, the classifier compares the article-implied chronology extracted by the LLM with the evidence-derived chronology to reveal global temporal conflicts. DelSA outperforms existing methods on ChronoFake, while remaining competitive on PolitiFact and GossipCop.

authors.name: Min Gao
authors.institution: Shanxi University of Finance and Economics

authors.name: Wentao Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Omni-IGN: Onboard Image-Goal Navigation for Drones with Omnidirectional Vision
papers.abstract: Image-goal navigation (ImageNav) requires an agent to reach a location specified by a goal image in an unknown environment. For drones, this task demands exploration, goal- directed navigation, and collision avoidance under limited onboard computing resources. Existing aerial ImageNav methods are built on single-view observations, requiring additional rotation and exploration to search for goal-relevant cues outside the field of view. In this paper, we present Omni-IGN, a fully onboard ImageNav system that integrates quad-fisheye perception, an attention-based reinforcement learning (RL) policy, and a collision-aware safety layer. The policy adaptively fuses goal-relevant features across multiple views to provide directional guidance for continuous navigation. The quad-fisheye RGB images support both ImageNav and obstacle avoidance without a dedicated depth sensor. On Habitat benchmarks, Omni-IGN achieves the best performance among continuous-action baselines. Moreover, flight tests in IsaacSim validate the effectiveness of integrating learning-based depth estimation with the action safety layer for collision avoidance. Finally, real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer without any fine-tuning or external localization. The code and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Shenao Wang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lin Zhao
authors.institution: Northwest Institute of Eco-Environment and Resources

papers.title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. In this scenario, existing systems (1) overlook tool-return readiness in service evaluation, wasting limited resources, and (2) use heuristic strategies to decide admission and placement on GPUs, resulting in suboptimal scheduling decisions. To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving. Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay, and token footprint; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.

papers.title: Peers4U: Designing Learner-Centered Virtual Peers for Children's Multimodal Mathematics Learning
papers.abstract: In early mathematics, children learn abstract concepts through concrete representations, such as manipulating objects, drawing, and speaking. Learning with peers can enrich this process by exposing children to diverse strategies and enabling them to exchange ideas through interaction. We realized this potential with virtual peers in Peers4U, a multimodal learning system to enhance children's mathematical conceptual understanding. Virtual peers driven by LLMs are personalized to the learner's cognitive level and assigned multimodal solutions with inspectable processes. During learning, peers engage in mixed-initiative interactions by responding, initiating topics, and advancing discussions along a pedagogical progression. A user study with 22 children and two experts showed our learner-centered topic orchestration significantly outperformed a persona-centered baseline, and children spontaneously authored new artifacts to demonstrate inspired ideas or share their own strategies, producing significantly more solutions when grouped with more Leading Peers. We contribute design insights for multimodal, learner-centered virtual peer systems.

authors.name: Lan Luo
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Chun Yu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Understanding Human-Robot Collaboration through Joint Action
papers.abstract: Human-robot collaboration requires partners to coordinate interdependent contributions toward a shared goal. Joint Action theory provides concepts for understanding this coordination, but how these concepts are instantiated and combined across empirical research remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA 2020, identifying 83 empirical papers published between 2021 and 2026. Through theory-driven framework analysis, we organized the literature into nine constructs across three capacities: Representation, Prediction, and Integration. We analyze how these constructs are distributed and co-occur across studies, revealing where empirical evidence concentrates and where it is absent. By mapping empirical HRC research onto a unified Joint Action framework, this review offers a coherent overview of HRC studies, identifies gaps in current evidence, and provides guidelines for future research.

authors.name: Jianyang Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Chun Yu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments
papers.abstract: Claims about the cognitive capabilities of large language models are typically tested by translating behavioral paradigms into text prompts, bypassing the visual interfaces and time pressure through which human participants actually engage with experiments. At the same time, AI agents can now complete online behavioral tasks and produce human-like data, which raises concerns that online datasets in the social and behavioral sciences are increasingly open to contamination. We introduce CogArena, a benchmark of ten experimental paradigms from the social and behavioral sciences. Agents complete the experiments through a standard web browser, working with the same visual stimuli and response interfaces that online participants use. A three-level scoring procedure evaluates whether the agent completed the task, how accurately it performed, and whether its data show the behavioral signatures each paradigm reliably produces in people. Across four multimodal models, each run ten times per task, we find that finishing an experiment and reproducing its signatures are different things. Many sessions did not finish, and those that did reproduced some signatures reliably and others not at all. CogArena provides the tasks, scoring code, and a public leaderboard for new submissions.

authors.name: Jialu Zhou
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Function spaces with compact-open topology need not be sober
papers.abstract: We exhibit sober spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that the function space $[X \to Y]_K$ of continuous maps, equipped with the compact-open topology, is not sober; the codomain can be chosen to be the Sierpi\'nski space $S$. Our construction builds on Isbell's complete lattice $M$, whose Scott space $\Sigma M$ is non-sober. Let $H = Q(M)$ be the set of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $\Sigma M$, ordered by reverse inclusion. Since $H$ is well known to be a spatial frame, the space $X = \mathrm{pt}(H)$ is sober with $\mathcal{O}(X) \cong H$. The key technical result is that sobriety of the space $H$ would entail sobriety of the original Scott space $\Sigma M$. This contradicts Isbell's example, and the desired counterexample follows.

authors.name: Bei Liu
authors.institution: The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center – Arthur G. James Cancer Hospital and Richard J. Solove Research Institute

papers.title: Attenuation of shoaling extreme wave crests by artificial salt marshes
papers.abstract: Laboratory experiments in a wave flume investigated the attenuation of shoaling extreme waves by artificial salt marshes placed immediately before an abrupt depth transition. Increasing vegetation density systematically reduced the excess kurtosis of the surface elevation distribution in the intermediate water depth regime. Nonetheless, attenuation exhibits a short saturation regime at low vegetation densities, whereas at very high densities, excess kurtosis decreases significantly across the gauges. However, kurtosis attenuation becomes ineffective as waves approach shallow-water conditions or as second-order nonlinear effects become significant. Furthermore, the highest experimental densities where the kurtosis is tamed exceed typical natural salt marsh stem densities. Thus, in natural settings, salt marshes are likely to provide only partial mitigation of extreme wave statistics in intermediate and shallow water depths, as the wave field retains some hazardous nonlinearity.

authors.name: Sahana Mahesh
authors.institution: JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research

authors.name: Gun Kim
authors.institution: Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology

papers.title: Continue or Restart? The Limits of Early Failure Prediction in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Early stopping promises to reduce compute costs for autonomous coding agents by terminating unpromising runs early. Deciding when to abandon a run requires separating baseline issue difficulty from the trajectory of an individual attempt. We study the distinction in 147,002 execution traces from two public corpora spanning four model-framework settings. Comparing pre-execution issue context against early execution prefixes, we evaluate linear count models, initial-turn text embeddings, task-conditional rankers, and a fine-tuned Qwen3-0.6B monitor. Although early prefixes modestly improve cross-task outcome ranking, within-task discrimination remains near chance across early landmarks (5k-20k tokens): initial-turn embeddings and 20k-token task-conditional models yield AUCs around 0.50, and three-seed neural evaluations across 32,406 attempts at 20k tokens achieve a mean within-task AUC of 0.50 [0.48, 0.51] across tasks of varying solve rates. To evaluate how these predictions translate into stopping decisions, we replay score-guided and matched random restarts under shared token budgets alongside uninterrupted continuation. Under a 75k-token cap, learned restarting improves resolution over matched random restarting by up to 1.98 percentage points. An exact algebraic decomposition resolves this paradox: the gain over random restarting stems almost entirely from between-task stopping allocation (avoiding stops on easy issues), whereas attempt-level selection within a task contributes near zero (-0.11 to +0.24 percentage points). Across all four settings at the 75k cap (and 216 of 224 tested budget-threshold configurations overall), uninterrupted continuation achieves higher solve rates at lower mean token cost than both restart policies. Practical evaluations of early stopping must therefore establish attempt-level discrimination and demonstrate net compute savings relative to continuation.

papers.title: Degrading the Grade: Grading Variance as Evidence of Shirking
papers.abstract: Variation in grading standards across instructors who teach the same students is evidence of a moral hazard problem, whether or not grades are inflated. The optimal standard is the same for every section of a course, yet grades vary widely across sections. We present a principal-agent model in which instructors who know the optimal standard still depart from it, leniently or harshly, depending on their incentives. Penalizing deviations from the department average leaves the average unchanged but compresses grading variance, which raises student welfare. Disclosing the same information to students instead increases grading variance.

papers.title: Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius
papers.abstract: For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][\Phi_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $\Phi_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials. In particular, no localization obtained by inverting finitely many nonzero Laurent polynomials suffices in this family.

papers.title: Explicit Regional Representations For Video Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: End-to-end video quality assessment (VQA) methods leave the regional evidence underlying their predictions largely implicit. We introduce an explicit pixel-level regional representation for VQA, instantiated as a Quality-Relevance Heatmap (QRH) that combines localized degradation evidence with perceptual priors under vision-language model guidance, without requiring pixel-level annotations. We apply QRH to existing VQA models through two deterministic fragment-sampling strategies: distribution-preserving sampling approximates the original sampler's QRH-score distribution without retraining, while quality-aware sampling prioritizes regions with high QRH scores and is paired with fine-tuning. Experiments with DOVER on multiple benchmarks show that the former closely approximates predictions averaged over random samples, while the latter improves most evaluated metrics across popular VQA benchmarks. These results support explicit regional representations as a useful interface for downstream VQA.

authors.name: Chenyu Wei
authors.institution: Hunan Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: LESSRec: Level-Specific History Modeling for Semantic ID-Based Recommendation
papers.abstract: Semantic ID-based recommendation represents each item as a sequence of semantic tokens obtained through residual quantization. This paradigm generates the next item's tokens autoregressively from coarse to fine, entailing each prediction attending to historical tokens at all semantic levels. However, our inference-time analysis reveals that historical tokens at the target-token's semantic level tend to be more informative, whereas other levels can introduce interference. Motivated by these findings, we propose LESSRec that separately encodes the historical token sequence at each semantic level and restricts attention over historical tokens to the sequence at the target token's semantic level during prediction. To complement these level-specific histories, LESSRec explicitly provides an item-level semantic sequence that represents each historical item's overall semantics in chronological order. The decoder accesses the level-aligned token sequence and the item-level semantic sequence through two separate cross-attention branches and fuses their contexts. We further introduce LESSRec+, which uses separate encoders for different semantic-level histories with the same total parameter count to reduce encoder computation. Extensive experiments across three public datasets and three tokenizers demonstrate the recommendation effectiveness of LESSRec and LESSRec+, with efficiency analyses highlighting the computational benefits of LESSRec+.

authors.name: Min Gao
authors.institution: Shanxi University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Local regularity for solutions to singular and degenerate quasilinear parabolic equations
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to prove local H\"{o}lder continuity for weak solutions to quasilinear parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type under finite integrability assumptions on the forcing, covering the supercritical singular range and the entire degenerate regime. The key ingredient is an $L^\infty$-valued temporal H\"{o}lder estimate of the solution after any fixed positive waiting time, which is achieved by coupling a time-rescaling argument with De Giorgi iteration. We also provide counterexamples involving forcing terms with weaker spatial integrability to show that even bounded continuous solutions with compatible data may possess no positive temporal H\"{o}lder exponent. In particular, these examples establish the sharpness of the spatial integrability threshold in the degenerate case. Finally, a separate counterexample is constructed to demonstrate that the temporal Lipschitz endpoint can fail for bounded continuous forcing when it depends on time.

papers.title: Approaching Optimal Scaling of Queue Size for an Input-Queued Switch
papers.abstract: We study the scaling of the expected total queue length in an $n\times n$ input-queued switch. It has been conjectured that the optimal scaling is $O(n/(1-\rho))$, up to logarithmic factors, where $\rho$ is the system load. This conjecture has been established in the traditional heavy-traffic regime and in certain sub-regimes of the large-system regime. But it remains unresolved over a wide range of load scalings in the large-system regime. In this paper, we develop a family of scheduling policies parameterized by a positive integer $k\ge 2$. We show that under uniform traffic, our policy achieves an expected total queue length of $O\bigl({n\log\max\{n,1/(1-\rho)\}}\big/{(1-\rho)^{2^k/(2^k-1)}}\bigr)$, as long as $\rho\to 1$ in the large-system regime. As $k$ increases, the exponent $2^k/(2^k-1)$ approaches $1$, bringing our bound arbitrarily close to the conjectured scaling. The expected amortized scheduling cost of the policy is $O(n^3 k)$ per time slot. Our policy is of a batching type, with a novel recursive design that allows an arbitrary number of batching levels. This design principle may also be useful for other scheduling problems in which combinatorial constraints restrict which jobs can be served simultaneously.

papers.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
papers.abstract: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement quality evaluation beyond off-the-shelf capability. We present MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that supplements LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria and evaluated against off-the-shelf baselines on an expert-labeled NASA requirement set using Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the open-weight Gemma 3 12B, with 100 executions per model. MARQ achieves median F1 scores of 0.80 for Claude Opus 5, 0.62 for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 0.53 for Gemma 3 12B, compared with off-the-shelf baselines of 0.55, 0.52, and 0.18, respectively. However, the nature of these gains is model-dependent. Claude Opus 5 improves defect detection and false-alarm control; GPT-5.6 Sol gains detection and better execution-level consistency at the cost of more false alarms; and Gemma 3 12B reaches the performance of off-the-shelf proprietary models, although it remains highly variable. Criterion-level analysis shows gains concentrated in Correctness and Conformance, trade-offs between misses and false alarms within individual criteria, and model-dependent responses across several criteria. These findings position SE knowledge infusion as a promising model-agnostic pathway for strengthening trustworthy LLM-based RE support while underscoring the need for criterion-specific interventions and human-in-the-loop review.

papers.title: An SRG/eROSITA Study of Be X-ray binaries in Quiescence
papers.abstract: Be X-ray binaries (BeXRBs) are mostly transient X-ray binaries with usually a neutron star as the compact object and a Be star as their optical companion. We performed a comprehensive analysis of BeXRBs in quiescence with the extended ROentgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array (eROSITA), the soft X-ray instrument on board the Spectrum-Roentgen-Gamma satellite, using its first all-sky survey (eRASS1) data. The transient BeXRBs spend majority of time in their quiescent state, but are often studied during their outbursts. A quiescence study is useful to probe the emission mechanism of BeXRBs at low mass accretion rates. The spectra of BeXRBs detected in the eRASS1 main catalogue could be well fitted with a powerlaw as well as a blackbody model. In the absence of detection of a BeXRB, we report the luminosity upper limit for its position in the sky. The X-ray luminosity for the quiescent BeXRBs detected with eROSITA have $L_{X}\sim10^{33-36}$ erg s$^{-1}$ for both absorbed powerlaw and blackbody models in most cases. For the absorbed blackbody model, the emission seems to come from a fraction of the neutron star's surface. The quiescence luminosity of BeXRBs are used to distinguish between different accretion models at low mass accretion rates, like accretion in the propeller regime or from a cold accretion disc. The detection space of BeXRBs in quiescence for the eRASS1 data is compared against previously reported luminosities across multiple X-ray observatories.

papers.title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
papers.abstract: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through executable harnesses that govern tool use and feedback. Optimizing a harness for a fixed policy overlooks how its behavior changes during learning, while training a policy under a fixed harness leaves the interface that generates its training experience unchanged. This motivates adapting the harness throughout policy training. We introduce CoHARL, a population-based reinforcement learning framework that co-evolves a shared policy and a population of executable harnesses. The policy learns from rollouts across the population, and a proposer uses its execution traces to revise harness code during training. CoHARL achieves a 27.6% mean resolved rate on SWE-rebench, improving over harness-only search by 6.4 percentage points. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show gains in software engineering and terminal-based tasks. Under matched training budgets, CoHARL also outperforms searching for a harness once before RL and alternating policy updates with revisions to a single active harness.

papers.title: TopoField: Technical Report for ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge
papers.abstract: Functional segmentation requires locating small interactive parts, such as knobs, buttons, and sockets, in indoor point clouds and returning confidence-ranked instance masks. A point-wise semantic predictor produces a continuous probability field, whereas the benchmark evaluates a discrete set of scored instances. This creates a substantial field-to-instance gap. We present TopoField, a deterministic decoder built on top of VOLT. TopoField first converts 13 test-time forward passes into a semantic consensus field, then decodes instance candidates from the consensus geometry, and finally ranks the candidates in a class-aware manner. The augmentation stage retains the processed-point identity of every fragment prediction, accumulates probabilities in a common point array, normalizes by coverage count, and fuses the resulting caches. The decoding stage separates high-confidence cores from broader support regions, constructs a symmetric radius-pruned point graph, and uses a multi-source graph-geodesic partition to split support regions that contain multiple seeds. On 561 ground-truth instances across 30 validation scenes, an IoU-0.5-valid candidate exists for 67.2% of instances, and top-1 coverage is 20.0%. These complementary measurements motivate joint attention to candidate construction and ranking. TopoField achieves 28.286% AP, 41.383% AP50, and 47.558% AP25. TopoField achieved second place on the ECCV 2026 SceneFun3D Challenge.

papers.title: Privately Clipping Heavy-Tailed Data
papers.abstract: Summing vectors is a basic task in differentially private data analysis. Standard private sum algorithms clip vectors to some bound, sum them, and add noise scaled to the bound. The differential privacy literature has developed a deep library of noise addition mechanisms, but it offers few tools for privately choosing a clipping bound based on the data. We introduce a method that privately chooses a clipping bound by optimizing residual coherence, the directional alignment of vectors exceeding the bound, against the variance cost of additional noise. We prove a close relationship between residual coherence and bias for a general class of heavy-tailed data regimes and show empirically that, across several datasets, our method outperforms existing baselines.

papers.title: LLM Hallucination Detection via Low-rank Multilinear Decomposition
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate fluent yet factually incorrect responses, raising concerns about their reliability. Recent hallucination detectors increasingly exploit internal representations, but extracting informative signals from high-dimensional hidden states remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on selected activations or pooling-based compression, potentially overlooking discriminative information distributed across Transformer layers, feature modes, and tokens. We propose LOTUS (Low-rank Order-statistic TUcker-based Subspace learning), a multilinear low-rank decomposition framework for hallucination detection that extracts compact representations from LLM hidden states while reducing dependence on labeled data. Our approach first summarizes variable-length token representations using complementary statistical descriptors that capture peak activations, activation distributions, and cross-layer changes. We then leverage low-rank multilinear decomposition to extract compact representations that capture the underlying structure of LLM hidden states, which are subsequently used to train a lightweight hallucination classifier. Experiments across multiple LLMs and question-answering benchmarks demonstrate improved hallucination detection performance over recent state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Underdamped Anchored Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Classical Langevin Monte Carlo algorithms, such as the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA), are based on discretization schemes of the overdamped Langevin dynamics and are widely used for sampling in machine learning because they scale to high dimensions and large datasets. However, they require differentiable log-densities, and are less efficient for sampling heavy-tailed distributions. Although various approaches have been proposed in the literature for sampling non-differentiable and heavy-tailed targets, all of them are developed in the overdamped setting only. We propose a novel momentum-based underdamped anchored Langevin dynamics (UALD), and underdamped anchored Langevin Monte Carlo (UALMC) algorithm based on a discretization scheme of UALD. Our paper is the first to provide a kinetic (momentum-based) Langevin algorithm for non-differentiable and heavy-tailed targets that is free of asymptotic bias. The method replaces the original potential with a smooth reference potential and modifies the underdamped Langevin dynamics via multiplicative scaling in the drift term. We establish non-asymptotic guarantees in the 2-Wasserstein distance to the target distribution and show that the resulting iteration complexity has better dependence on dimension and accuracy level compared to overdamped-based anchored Langevin algorithms. We provide numerical experiments to illustrate the theory and practical performance of our proposed approach.

papers.title: Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves language-model post-training by letting the student learn from its own sampled trajectories under teacher supervision, aligning the training process with inference-time behavior. However, the rollout policy in OPD is usually treated as fixed: each round samples directly from the current student. We show that this choice can create a compounding teacher--student mismatch, because it requires the teacher to provide effective supervision on whichever trajectories the student samples, including ones less reachable by the teacher itself. On such trajectories, teacher supervision can become noisy or even misleading, leading to undesirable student patterns such as repetition. Moreover, since the updated student in turn defines the rollout policy of subsequent rounds, these patterns persist and potentially amplify over training. This failure mode suggests that improving OPD requires treating the rollout policy itself as an optimization target, rather than only modifying the distillation objective. We propose Mixture Proposal On-Policy Distillation (MPOPD), which derives a student-anchored, teacher-guided rollout distribution from a local trust-region objective based on relative teacher support. The resulting target is a geometric mixture of the student and teacher policies, and we introduce a proposal policy that approximates this mixture, enabling rollout generation in a single forward pass. Experiments on 16 math, knowledge, and medical reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over OPD and recent variants. On math reasoning, our method improves average accuracy by 6.91 over OPD on Qwen3-4B-Base while reducing average generation length by 41%, suggesting that rollout policy design provides an effective way to improve OPD.

papers.title: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: We propose HiLo-RD (High-to-Low Budget Representation Distillation) to improve masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) under a limited generation budget. Unlike autoregressive models, MDLMs choose both what to generate and where to commit it. This creates two coupled challenges: predicting useful content before reasoning is complete, and deciding when to fix answer tokens that shape later predictions. We identify budget-induced premature commitment: even when a correct solution fits, the model can fix answer fragments near the window boundary before resolving intermediate steps. These fragments become context for later predictions and redirect subsequent reasoning. Existing post-training methods do not directly transfer the stronger trajectories that the same model follows with a larger window. HiLo-RD addresses this gap by (1) pairing large-window teacher states with cropped small-window views and (2) matching their hidden representations at committed positions. This supervision guides both token prediction and commitment order without an external teacher. Across mathematics benchmarks, HiLo-RD improves low-budget accuracy and shortens responses; these gains extend to code generation without code-domain training. On GSM8K, accuracy rises by 9.4 percentage points as mean readable length falls by about 25%. Attention diagnostics and fixed-budget order interventions support the proposed mechanism. Together, these results show that large-window reasoning can improve small-window decoding.

papers.title: Dynamical systems analysis of Bianchi type-IX cosmology with a scalar field mediated dark sector interaction
papers.abstract: The recent DESI DR2 results preference for a time-varying dark-energy equation of state, together with the long-standing difficulty of explaining why an initially anisotropic universe should evolve toward isotropy, motivates the study of interacting dark-sector models in anisotropic backgrounds. We investigate the dynamics of Bianchi type-IX cosmologies containing pressureless dark matter coupled to dark energy in the form of a quintessence scalar field $\phi$ with exponential potential $V(\phi)=V_0\,e^{-\lambda\phi}$. Energy exchange between the two dark components is mediated by the scalar field through the interaction term $Q=\kappa\beta\dot\phi\,\rho_{\rm DM}$, where $\kappa^2=8\pi G$ and $\beta$ is a dimensionless coupling. Because Bianchi~IX models generically recollapse, the Hubble scalar $H$ vanishes at the moment of maximum expansion, where the expansion-normalized variables of the standard Wainwright--Ellis formalism diverge. We therefore adopt the $D$-normalized phase-space formalism of Hewitt, Uggla, and Wainwright, which compactifies the state space and remains regular through the recollapse, including the moment of maximum expansion at which $H = 0$. Together with the modified conservation equations for the two dark components, the Einstein equation reduces to a closed autonomous polynomial dynamical system, whose fixed points we classify by linear stability analysis, supplemented by center-manifold theory for the non-hyperbolic points. The fixed points shows the kinetic-dominated, coupling modified matter dominated, curvature scalar, scalar field dominated and coupled scaling families; the last is the anisotropic analogue of the Amendola scaling attractor. Restricting to the initially expanding, isotropizing trajectories, we map the region of the $(\lambda,\beta)$ plane in which anisotropic Bianchi~IX models approach an accelerating Friedmann--Robertson--Walker state.

papers.title: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) characterizes dependence between two regions conditioned on an intervening buffer. Its characteristic decay length, the Markov length, has recently been identified as a diverging length scale at mixed-state phase transitions. Here, we investigate CMI dynamics in one-dimensional classical stochastic models and propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length diverges with time. We derive this form in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation, where domain-wall coarsening generates a growing length scale and a self-similar probability distribution. We introduce a Hankel-based truncation scheme that enables matrix-product-state simulations at long times and over large spatial regions. Using this method, we verify the proposed scaling both in the inactive phase and at the nonequilibrium critical point, where the dynamical critical exponent governs Markov-length growth. More broadly, the same scaling form captures cases in which collective inference sets the diverging Markov length. Despite these distinct mechanisms, the CMI between fixed microscopic regions exhibits a common scaling dimension of two. Finally, we extend this framework to temporal CMI, establishing an analogous relation between the strength of conditional dependence in time domain and its characteristic memory time.

papers.title: $O(3)$-symmetry of four-dimensional steady Ricci solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete connected four-dimensional gradient steady Ricci soliton with positive curvature operator that is $\kappa$-noncollapsed at all scales admits an effective isometric $O(3)$ action preserving the potential function and having principal orbits diffeomorphic to $S^2$.

papers.title: Highest weight vectors in queer Howe duality
papers.abstract: We use Gauss decomposition to study the singular vectors in the regular representation on the coordinate superalgebra of the big cell of the queer supergroup. This gives explicit bases for the highest weight spaces in queer Howe duality. As an application, the same method recovers the explicit highest weight vectors in the general linear case obtained by Cheng and Wang.

papers.title: Operator Barron Regularity for Elliptic Equations and Application to Neural Operator Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a spectral Barron regularity framework for nonlinear operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces. Using Hilbert-valued Fourier representations of finite-dimensional input truncations, we establish bounds that are uniform in the input truncation dimension and prove arbitrary-order Barron regularity for a class of elliptic solution operators. Second, we use this operator Barron regularity to derive approximation error bounds for an FNO-type neural operator, with explicit dependence on the input truncation dimension, output reconstruction dimension, and network width. For a fixed input truncation dimension, optimizing the neural approximation bound over the Barron regularity order yields stretched-exponential decay of the approximation error in the network width. We also show some numerical experiments to support the predicted rate.

papers.title: SpecGuard: Detecting Multi-Turn LLM Jailbreaks via Specification-Based Runtime Monitoring
papers.abstract: Multi-turn jailbreaks turn dialogue safety into a trace property: a violation may become identifiable only when user intent and assistant behavior are considered across multiple turns. Existing guard models largely classify individual messages or exchanges and return risk scores or labels, without executable safety semantics or a formally checkable decision trail. We present SpecGuard, a training-free, specification-driven framework for monitoring multi-turn LLM interactions. SpecGuard uses a fixed atomic-proposition contract to map natural-language observations into causally scoped, evidence-backed facts, and expresses forbidden interaction patterns as Linear Temporal Logic specifications. Each specification is compiled into a symbolic finite automaton that incrementally consumes the resulting dialogue trace. The same monitoring mechanism supports buffered runtime checking and retrospective auditing, while accepting runs produce replayable witnesses that identify the triggered specification, supporting facts, and relevant dialogue turns. Experiments on multi-turn safety benchmarks show that SpecGuard consistently outperforms representative open-source guard models while maintaining controlled false-positive rates. These results demonstrate a practical path from heuristic risk classification toward formally specified, verifiable, and auditable LLM safety monitoring, without learned detector parameters or access to the protected model.

papers.title: Minimax Rates for Robust Gaussian Mean Estimation Near the Breakdown Point under Constraints
GeoGSplat: Geometry-Grounded Non-Pixel-Aligned Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting enables efficient novel view synthesis, but pixel-aligned prediction makes the primitive count grow with image resolution and view count, leading to substantial redundancy and increased computational cost. Non-pixel-aligned methods address this limitation by predicting a fixed number of Gaussians. Without explicit ray and depth constraints, these methods yield misplaced Gaussian centers, causing rendering artifacts under large viewpoint changes. To address this issue, we introduce GeoGSplat, a geometry-grounded feed-forward model that explicitly incorporates geometric priors into the non-pixel-aligned framework. A dual-branch encoder constructs Anchors and Triplane to capture coarse 3D structure and fine-grained scene features, respectively. Subsequently, a hierarchical decoder progressively decodes dense 3D points and Gaussian primitives, enabling 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis. GeoGSplat surpasses both state-of-the-art pixel-aligned and non-pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting methods on DTU and NRGBD in terms of novel view synthesis and reconstruction. The advantage of our geometry-grounded paradigm further increases as target viewpoints move farther from the input cameras, demonstrating stronger generalization to large viewpoint changes. Project Page: https://comedy0913.github.io/projects/geogsplat

papers.title: Deep Holes and Aperture: Sign Laws for the Empirical Correlation of Lattice-Sampled Random Wave Fields
papers.abstract: A Gaussian random wave field is sampled on a lattice within a bounded aperture. After displacement, re-indexing leaves a residual in the Voronoi cell. We study whether the empirical lag correlation has positive real part throughout the cell. For each realization in a single-output reciprocal link with noiseless over-the-air return, this is equivalent to the negative returned gradient being a descent direction for all residuals and differentiable losses with nonzero error signals. Return noise is treated exactly. For isotropic fields, ball-shaped apertures, unshifted lattice points, and dilations approaching the critical covering radius, every minimizer is a deep hole except with exponentially small probability. A Gaussian vector on the deep holes determines the limiting failure probability, with explicit covariance and lattice-independent limiting normalization. Square, hexagonal, simple cubic, and body-centered cubic lattices have two, three, four, and twelve sign classes. At fixed target failure probabilities below the critical limiting value, this covariance determines the exact leading aperture constant. When the margin and target failure probability vanish jointly, that constant is common to lattice shapes within each dimension. A cubic correction yields vanishing relative tail error in a moderate-deviation regime. A non-asymptotic two-sided aperture law has explicit constants. With a Rayleigh-faded specular path and positive diffuse margin, a failure floor occurs at every positive path power exactly when the cosine of its phase change is negative somewhere in the cell. The floor vanishes for all directions exactly when the covering radius is at most a quarter wavelength.

papers.title: Negative Results for Reciprocity-Based Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging: Stability, Alignment, and Geometry
papers.abstract: In reciprocity-based over-the-air split learning, channel aging rotates and attenuates the derivative signal returned to the transmitter. Seven case studies combine numerical forecasts, mechanism checks, and competing predictions. Near the correlation zero, an archived SGD comparison finds truncated inversion 0.000813 lower in cross-entropy than polar correction, with a paired 95% interval for the difference from -0.001853 to 0.000060, and a retained-mode quadratic proxy slightly favors truncation. Selecting the return port with the largest received power falls short of the predicted five-point alignment advantage over random selection at both tested spacings, gaining at most 0.97 points, while the local inverse relation between amplitude and phase gradient is supported. Seven specified interference-induced accuracy-collapse predictions are rejected, and independent zero-mean interference preserves the conditional mean under a fixed linear chain. Per-subcarrier correction and spherical-wavefront compensation do not deliver their predicted accuracy gains. Focusing leaves both methods near chance in a single-mode model and adds no observed gain in a model with a line-of-sight component plus scattering. A successful port assignment under nonsymmetric motion refutes an exact-symmetry requirement. The competing positioning-error prediction is supported. Gaussian rail jitter with a standard deviation of 0.383 wavelengths yields high terminal test accuracy, whereas a fixed bias of the same magnitude yields near-chance accuracy. These cases distinguish valid local physical relations from unsupported training forecasts through task support, noise injection, and update moments.

papers.title: Global minimax rates for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation
papers.abstract: Recent work established minimax rates for pointwise estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE), but the fundamental limits under global losses remained unresolved. We derive matching minimax lower and upper bounds under the $L_2$ and $L_\infty$ risks on certain covariate-density and support classes. For the lower bounds, we develop a many-fuzzy-hypotheses method that replaces each fixed alternative in a multiple-hypothesis construction with a mixture over nuisance functions that leaves its CATE unchanged. A localized product-mixture $\chi^2$ bound is used to control the divergence of each resulting mixture from a common baseline, enabling multiple well-separated CATE hypotheses to be handled simultaneously. For the upper bounds, we analyze a modified local polynomial R-learner. The $L_2$ argument extends the pointwise bias--variance analysis, while the $L_\infty$ argument combines concentration inequalities for U-statistics with a continuity argument enabled by the use of a continuous kernel and additional regularity of the second-order basis. The resulting rates show that the pointwise elbow phenomenon persists globally: the $L_2$ transition threshold is unchanged, while the $L_\infty$ rate has an additional logarithmic factor and a transition threshold adjusted by $1-\log\log n/\log n$.

papers.title: A Theory of Transmit-Receive-Manifold of Single-Photon Quantum-Dot Antenna Arrays
papers.abstract: A quantum-dot array that receives a single photon is a collectively coupled antenna, and its receive manifold is not always the plane-wave manifold. So, this work aims to develop a complete transmit-channel-receive manifold model for quantum dot (QD) arrays. For the sake of validation, it considers a reference target pattern which can be obtained using classical array excitation.

papers.title: Lipi-Ghor: A Large-Scale, Diarized, Multi-Domain Bengali Speech Corpus and a Scalable Pipeline for Building It
papers.abstract:
Bengali, spoken by over 230 million people, remains severely under-resourced in spoken language research. Existing open Bengali ASR corpora are confined to short, read or crowd-sourced speech and lack speaker diarization and long-form audio.
  We present Lipi-Ghor, a large-scale weakly-supervised Bengali speech corpus comprising 885 hours of audio sourced from 998 YouTube videos across 596 unique channels, spanning 17 diverse domains including audiobooks, drama, religious sermons, news, and regional dialects. Each recording is annotated in SSTT format (Speaker, Speech, Transcription, Timestamp), which combines automated diarization with Bengali YouTube caption tracks.
  To our knowledge, Lipi-Ghor is the first Bengali speech corpus to pair large-scale coverage with speaker-diarized, long-form audio annotations, both of which are absent from existing open Bengali resources. We also present the construction methodology as a replicable pipeline for any language with a sufficient captioned YouTube presence. Targeted channel curation across a handful of rich domains yields corpus scales that were previously out of reach for low-resource languages.
  We benchmark four widely-used ASR models under zero-shot and fine-tuned conditions. All four degrade consistently on emotive, dialectal, and long-form content. Because caption targets are noisy, we also release a human-annotated gold evaluation split, verified by 17 volunteer annotators over 30 hours of human-in-the-loop correction and stratified across all 17 domains.
  We release our original contributions (video-ID lists, diarization output, pipeline code, and the gold annotations) under CC-BY-4.0, and distribute caption-derived transcripts for research use only; no raw audio is redistributed.

papers.title: Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
papers.abstract: DNA methylation (DNAM) array-based tumor classification is a powerful clinical diagnostic tool, but models trained on fixed reference cohorts can produce faulty predictions for tumor types not represented in the training distribution. We propose an end-to-end deep representation learning-based out-of-distribution (OOD) detection framework for DNAm array data. Deep neural network (DNN) classifiers were trained on public sarcoma (SARC) (GSE140686) and brain tumor (BT) (GSE90496) cohorts, and feature vectors were extracted from bottleneck layers. Five OOD methods, including 1dimension (1D)-Subspace Analysis (1D-SSA), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Ridge Regression, Mahalanobis Distance (MD), and Sum of Squared Distances (SSD), were explored with 200 and 500-dimensional embeddings. Spectral discrepancy was used to discriminate in-distribution (IND) from OOD samples. Performance was measured via cross-validation, holdout samples, and an independent clinical dataset. 1D-SSA was the most effective approach. In the sarcoma-IND/brain tumor-OOD setting, the framework achieved an AUROC of 0.975 and True Negative Rate (TNR)@95TPR of 0.930, and an AUROC of 0.9569 and TNR@95TPR of 0.8660 for the brain tumor-IND/sarcoma-OOD setting. On the independent clinical test set, the method yielded a mean AUROC of 0.976, a DE of 0.032, an FPR@95TPR of 0.065, and a TNR@95TPR of 0.935. These results show deep representation-based OOD detection as a practical quality-control layer for clinical-grade methylation-based tumor classification systems.

papers.title: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke
papers.abstract: Automated polysomnography after ischemic stroke is challenging because of altered sleep-related neural activity and concurrent respiratory disturbances. Existing stroke-specific approaches mainly address sleep-stage classification, leaving joint analysis of sleep architecture and respiratory events underexplored. Moreover, adapting pretrained EEG encoders introduces a representation inconsistency when downstream models are trained on embeddings from previously seen patients but evaluated on unseen individuals. We propose MM-Net, a multimodal multi-task framework that resolves this inconsistency through cross-fitting and ridge-based embedding alignment. Sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations and engineered neural descriptors are fused with learned cardiorespiratory features through cross-attention and shared temporal modeling for simultaneous sleep staging and respiratory-event detection. On iSLEEPS (99 patients with subacute ischemic stroke), ten-fold patient-independent evaluation achieved 76.3% staging accuracy (Cohen's $\kappa$ = 0.656) and 0.825 respiratory-event AUC, outperforming the evaluated baselines under matched protocols. The sleep-adapted encoder improved the downstream model when its embeddings were aligned, raising staging accuracy by 1.4 percentage points over the frozen encoder ($p$ = 0.020) versus 0.2 points without alignment. MM-Net also achieved 86.4% staging accuracy on Sleep-EDF, above every single-EEG architecture reimplemented on the same recordings, and 80.3% staging accuracy with 0.889 respiratory AUC on ISRUC-I, exceeding its retrained staging baselines. Without retraining, the iSLEEPS-trained model retained respiratory AUCs of 0.833 on ISRUC-I and 0.841 on UCD. These findings support representation-consistent neural adaptation and joint physiological modeling across stroke, healthy-sleep, and sleep-disorder cohorts.

papers.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
papers.abstract:
Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(\mu:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(\mu\), the symplectic quotient \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow \mu^{-1}(U_a)/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(U_a\) of \(a\). We define a formal Kirwan map
  \[
  \kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).
  \]
  We prove that \(\kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}\) is surjective under a local \emph{equivariant homotopy retraction} condition on the slice level sets
  \[
  C_x=\mu_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x,
  \]
  which is satisfied, for example, when \(a\) is a regular value of every slice moment map, or when \(a=0\) and \(C_x\) is a \(G_x\)-equivariant cone. The weakest condition we identify is the existence, for each \(x\in\mu^{-1}(a)\), of a local quasi-isomorphism
  \[
  \Car(S_x,G_x)\simeq \cC^\bullet_{C_x}
  \]
  in a \(G_x\)-equivariant neighborhood of the orbit, without requiring a global tubular neighborhood. As an application we recover, in the formal framework, the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

papers.title: Image-Domain CT Metal Artifact Reduction Using an Endpoint-Conditioned Diffusion Bridge
papers.abstract:
Background: Metal implants cause streaking and shading artifacts in computed tomography (CT), obscuring anatomy and distorting Hounsfield-unit (HU) values. Conventional diffusion models reconstruct images from Gaussian noise rather than directly exploiting anatomical information retained in artifact-corrupted CT.
  Purpose: To develop an image-domain metal artifact reduction (MAR) method connecting artifact-corrupted and metal-free CT images through an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge.
  Methods: The proposed RDBM-MAR method uses an endpoint-conditioned diffusion bridge and initializes reconstruction from the artifact CT image. A conditional U-Net predicts an image-domain correction from intermediate bridge states. Inference uses 10 deterministic reverse steps. We used 14,000 paired CT slices from the AAPM CT-MAR Grand Challenge, including 12,045 training, 633 validation, and 1,322 held-out test slices. One clinical benchmark case was assessed qualitatively. We compared RDBM-MAR with CycleGAN, Pix2Pix, Res-SRDiff, I2I-Mamba, and I2SB using PSNR, SSIM, MAE, and LPIPS. Statistical analysis used Friedman and paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm correction.
  Results: RDBM-MAR achieved the highest PSNR (43.67 +/- 4.56 dB) and SSIM (0.9856 +/- 0.0138) and the lowest MAE (14.74 +/- 8.68 HU). All four metrics differed significantly among methods (p < 0.001). RDBM-MAR outperformed all five comparators in PSNR, SSIM, and MAE (adjusted p < 0.001); Res-SRDiff achieved the lowest LPIPS. Difference maps, HU profiles, and the clinical case showed reduced artifacts with preservation of surrounding anatomy.
  Conclusions: RDBM-MAR provides a direct restoration trajectory from artifact CT toward metal-free CT, achieving strong structural fidelity and HU accuracy using 10 reverse steps.

authors.name: Xiaofeng Yang
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: On the Fundamental Limits of Bistatic ISAC Over Vector Channels
papers.abstract: This paper studies the fundamental limits of bistatic integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems over vector channels. We first consider a class of parallel channels in which, on each component channel, the channel from the transmitter (Tx) to the communication receiver (Rx) is degraded with respect to the channel from the Tx to the sensing Rx, or vice versa, where the direction of degradation may vary across component channels. For this class of channels, we establish matching achievability and converse results, which yield a single-letter characterization of the capacity-distortion function $C(D)$. For parallel Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, the evaluation of the capacity-distortion-power function $C(D,P)$ under the squared error distortion measure reduces to a joint power and distortion allocation problem across the component channels. We then extend the analysis to general vector channels and derive single-letter lower and upper bounds on $C(D)$. In particular, for vector Gaussian channels with additive Gaussian states, we prove the optimality of Gaussian superposition coding without requiring a global degradation order between the communication and sensing channels, by combining the channel enhancement technique with a matrix extremal inequality based on Fisher information. This leads to an exact characterization of $C(D,P)$.

papers.title: Counting by the Book: Verifying Alaska's Ranked-Choice Elections
papers.abstract: We present Alaska's ranked-choice elections as a case study in Formally Verified Democracy, a program to establish election results through formally checked proofs. We formalize an interpretation of Alaska's tabulation rules in Lean, verify its implementation, and prove election-specific results. Across 115 ranked-choice contests in Alaska since 2022, we identify 75 ballot records across 10 contests that were counted differently from this interpretation by a program reproducing the published results, without changing any winners. We trace these differences to overvotes and duplicate rankings and examine their legal justification, showing how formal verification can expose consequential choices in translating election law into software.

papers.title: Degree-truncated DP-colouring of $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract:
A graph $G$ is degree-truncated DP-$k$-colourable (respectively, degree-truncated $k$-choosable) if it is DP-$f$-colourable (respectively, $f$-choosable), where $f(v)=\min\{k,d_G(v)\}$ for every vertex $v$. Hutchinson proved that every $2$-connected maximal outerplanar graph other than the triangle is degree-truncated $5$-choosable. Lo, Wang, Zhou and Zhu strengthened this result by proving that every $2$-connected $K_{2,4}$-minor-free graph other than cycles and complete graphs is degree-truncated DP-$5$-colourable.
  Outerplanar graphs are precisely the $\{K_4,K_{2,3}\}$-minor-free graphs. We study how the truncation threshold grows when $K_{2,3}$ is replaced by $K_{2,t}$, while $K_4$-minor remains excluded. A bound independent of $t$ is impossible, as shown by the family $\{K_{2,n}| n\ge 2\}$. Let $\mathcal S_t$ be the class of $2$-connected $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs other than cycles. Writing $\chi^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t)$ for the least truncation threshold valid throughout this class, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge3$, \[ \left\lfloor2\sqrt{2t}\right\rfloor \le \chi^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t) \le \left\lceil4\sqrt{2t}\right\rceil. \]

papers.title: The Structure Gap: When More Data Cannot Replace Structured Reasoning
papers.abstract: A persistent belief in modern AI is that sufficiently large learners trained on sufficiently much data can make explicit domain knowledge optional. This paper examines a limitation of that belief. We define structure-encoded problems: tasks whose input-output map is determined, or sharply constrained, by known structure such as a solver, symmetry group, graph, physical law, measurement operator, grammar, combinatorial search space, or optimization objective. For such tasks, the central question is not expressivity--a dense neural network may contain the desired map--but finite-data identification, extrapolation, and certification. We introduce the structure gap: the finite-resource gap between a method that receives the governing structure and a learner that receives only examples. The strongest useful form of the claim is asymptotic rather than absolute: structure-agnostic learning may approach a structured solver as coverage grows, but every finite dataset can leave residual uncertainty that the structure resolves by construction. We prove this exactly for a Gaussian inverse problem: the known-operator Wiener solver attains Bayes risk, while the dense empirical learner in the correct linear class has persistent expected excess risk. We also prove a cell-coverage lower bound and an unobserved-orbit non-identifiability result. Controlled experiments in known-operator inversion, sparse recovery, and graph reachability with size extrapolation instantiate the mechanisms. When validated structure is available, it can constrain the hypothesis space before learning begins, leaving learning to address components the structure does not specify.

papers.title: No closed-form formula for Stiefel geodesics
papers.abstract: We use differential Galois theory to prove that given two arbitrary points $X$ and $Y$ on the Stiefel manifold, there is no closed-form analytic expression for the Riemannian logarithm $\log_X Y$, the geodesic between $X$ and $Y$, or the geodesic distance between $X$ and $Y$. In other words, these cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions of the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$; in fact, our result goes further --- even if we allow for repeated integrals of elementary functions, there is still no such expression.

papers.title: Let the Gate Decide: Per-Lookup Precision for Quantized Conditional Memory in LLMs
papers.abstract: Conditional memory layers, such as DeepSeek's Engram, attach large hashed n-gram tables to a language model, and removing them from DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash costs 36.8 PopQA points. Low-bit quantization loses long-tail facts first, and the standard remedy, giving more bits to frequently accessed rows, backfires: refining lookups by access frequency is worse than refining them at random. We trace this to the gate that scales each retrieved row. A lookup's quantization error is weighted by its gate, which is small for frequent n-grams, large for the rare n-grams of long-tail entities, and computable from a 1-bit code. GateRQ therefore stores each row as a ladder of 1-bit residual codes, keeps level 1 in GPU memory to compute the gate, and reads deeper levels only for the lookups the gate ranks highest. Without retraining, GateRQ cuts GPU table memory by 7.8x on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which raises vLLM throughput by 11%-31% over FP8 tables, while losing about 1 PopQA point at 1.50 bits read per lookup and 0.2 points at 2.10 bits across two models.

papers.title: A Smart Instant Book Filter Model based on Dual-Objective Optimization
papers.abstract:
Hospitality service in online marketplaces has become increasingly popular over the past few years, not only because it helps people easily rent short-term lodging but also because it empowers travelers to connect with locals and feel belonging. A typical pattern of these industries is a central platform mediating the economic interactions between guests and hosts, where a successful booking experience is the key to user satisfaction. However, one of the biggest challenges is the possible delay of response and chance of rejection when guests try to book a request-to-book listing. Previously, we enabled the instant book feature to allow hosts to instantly accept qualified guests and guests to confirm bookings immediately. Yet the symptom has not been alleviated given mixed request-to-book and instant book listing supply in search results. One possible solution is to promote all instant book listings in search results; however, booking rate will be damaged due to some improperly promoted low quality listings.
  In this paper, we present a novel smart instant book filter system that applies the instant book filter intelligently and shifts request-to-book to instant book without hurting booking rate. Compared with traditional two-sided markets research that targets finding strategies to maximize a single overall social welfare goal, our proposed system aims to maximize the instant book rate with the constraint that booking rate should not decrease, forming a dual-objective optimization problem.
  We show A/B testing results for our system exposed to global users, demonstrating that our model performs better than previous human-expert-tuned models in terms of both instant book rate and overall booking rate. We also achieved improved metrics such as the host instant book adoption rate. The proposed system has been deployed to production and is serving millions of users every day.

authors.name: Li Fan
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: SAGE: Saliency-Annealed Gated Encoder for Universal Vision Recognition
papers.abstract: When adapting self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs) to dense prediction, existing methods often treat the ViT as a passive feature extractor and may underuse the rich priors encoded in its representations, including saliency, global context, and high-frequency details. We propose SAGE (Saliency-Annealed Gated Encoder), an enhanced ViT-Adapter backbone that explicitly exploits these priors through three complementary innovations: (1) a saliency-guided architecture that extracts DINO-style class-token (CLS) saliency to guide feature gating and high-frequency enhancement, together with dynamic multi-layer aggregation and a local-detail branch; (2) an annealing-based training paradigm designed to improve convergence and feature quality during early training while reducing feature drift later in training; and (3) a two-stage, quality-aware training mechanism that smoothly transitions from focal loss to Varifocal Loss (VFL) within a single training run. Across the evaluated tasks (Fig.~\ref{fig:fig_com}), SAGE achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) or competitive results on COCO (62.8 box AP and 55.3 mask AP), COCO keypoint estimation (78.5 AP), ADE20K (60.3 mIoU for semantic segmentation and 44.9 mask AP for instance segmentation), TinyImageNet classification (94.76\% Top-1 accuracy), and DIOR-R oriented object detection (78.8 AP$_{50}$). The same backbone is used across tasks, with task-specific decoders. To the best of our knowledge, SAGE is the first framework to achieve multi-task state-of-the-art results on Huawei Ascend NPUs. Code and pretrained models will be released after internal review.

authors.name: Junyu Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications
