papers.title: Learning the solution operator of standing waves with a Fourier neural operator
papers.abstract: The standing wave problem concerns the space-time periodic motion at the free surface of a two-dimensional, infinitely deep, irrotational flow of an incompressible inviscid fluid under gravity. Although spectrally accurate computations have revealed a rich array of nonlinear wave phenomena, repeatedly evaluating their evolution over large parameter spaces remains challenging, particularly when resolving fine-scale spatial oscillations. We employ a Fourier neural operator (FNO) architecture to learn the solution operator along a numerically computed one-parameter family of symmetric standing waves. Given a wave profile at an instant of rest and a normalized observation time, the learned operator predicts the fluid surface, the velocity potential and the dipole density at the surface at that time. In-distribution tests yield uniformly small relative errors within the training range. Two out-of-distribution experiments characterize extrapolation toward contrasting physical regimes. Toward the free-fall limit, errors concentrate near the sharpening crest, consistent with the spectral truncation in the FNO architecture. Toward the linear limit, absolute errors remain small whereas relative errors increase as the amplitude vanishes. A residual of the governing equations, evaluated independently of reference solutions, complements these tests and provides a diagnostic for exploratory predictions beyond the available data.

papers.title: Laws of the iterated logarithm for the range of once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$
DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
papers.abstract: Unsteady flow over a 30 $\mu$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

papers.title: Persistent Hubs and Sharp Asymptotics in Eigenvector Preferential Attachment Trees
papers.abstract: We prove sharp almost-sure asymptotics for eigenvector preferential attachment trees in which each attachment uses eigenvector centrality with probability $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and uniform selection with probability $1-\alpha$. A unique persistent hub eventually has the maximum degree, which is asymptotic to $\gamma^2t^{2/3}$, where $\gamma=(9\alpha/10)^{1/3}$. The Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue is asymptotic to $\gamma t^{1/3}$, and the second-largest degree is asymptotic to $2\gamma t^{1/3}$. The hub and its neighbors each carry asymptotically half of the squared Perron mass. We also identify the centrality profile by degree and an explicit mixture of geometric laws for the degree of a uniformly sampled vertex. A limiting distance profile quantifies the dandelion geometry, and vertices beyond the hub's neighbors have maximum degree of order at most $\log t$.

papers.title: Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
papers.abstract:
Long-horizon coding tasks contain nested subtasks. Typically, agents record interactions sequentially into a growing history, causing context inflation and performance degradation. Compressing or trimming the history without explicit subtask boundaries can discard information needed by unfinished subtasks. Conversely, recursive subagent delegation isolates completed subtasks through child agents by assigning every subtask boundary to delegation, which conflates subtask granularity with executing agent choice, adding execution and coordination overhead. We introduce Spine, an interface and runtime that align model context with subtask nesting and completion. An agent declares explicit subtask boundaries through work scopes, allowing the same agent to execute nested subtasks inline while reserving delegation for independent parallel tasks. The runtime organizes execution in SpineTree, a persistent tree recording subtask relations, local interactions, completion states, and returned results. Before each model call, it compiles the tree into model context just in time, retaining unfinished subtasks' interactions and replacing completed subtasks' details with their results, while preserving prefix-cache reuse.
  We integrate Spine into Codex to build SpineCodex. With GPT-5.6 Sol, compared with native Codex, SpineCodex improves SWE-Milestone Score by 11.8% while reducing total cost by 32.4%, improves the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 17.3%, and improves Mean@5 on eight of the ten evaluated FrontierSWE tasks. On SWE-Milestone, it also achieves a comparable Score to Recursive Subagent at 73.7% lower total cost. We also integrate Spine into Pi through a reusable software package: with Gemini 3.8 Flash and Qwen 3.8 27B, it improves SWE-Milestone Score by 9.5-17.5% and the average ProgramBench test-pass rate by 4.3-8.7% compared with native Pi.

papers.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
papers.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. This cost becomes prohibitive for megapixel-scale frames with N_f~100. Although dynamic programming can reduce the computational complexity by a factor of N_f, it requires a prohibitive memory of O(N_x N_y N_f^2), unsuitable for large-format detectors. This article presents a novel algorithm to achieve the computational efficiency of dynamic programming while maintaining a memory footprint of just O(N_x N_y N_f) by slightly approximating the computation of frame shifts for alignment. By expressing the shift as a sum of terms proportional to the digits frame index in binary and rounding up each of these terms, frames can be integrated efficiently by hierarchically adding intermediate sums that are shared across different velocities with the same higher bits in binary. The approximation only introduces a small tracking error that increases logarithmically with the number of frames. This advancement enables synthetic tracking to be executed with high energy efficiency, making it practical for deployment on standard workstations rather than requiring high-performance computing infrastructure such as GPU servers or CPU clusters.

authors.name: Chengxing Zhai
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Data-driven stochastic reconstruction of dengue epidemic dynamics: state-dependent stochasticity and temporal organization
papers.abstract: Dengue epidemics exhibit strong stochastic variability, temporal memory and complex temporal organization that are difficult to capture using conventional deterministic epidemic models. However, the dependence of epidemic fluctuations on the underlying dynamical state and their influence on reconstruction across temporal scales remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we develop a data-driven stochastic framework to investigate dengue epidemic dynamics using daily infection data from Imphal West District, Manipur, India, for 2023-2025. We use Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) to separate deterministic and stochastic epidemic components. Logarithmic regression and autocorrelation analyses reveal empirically state-dependent noise amplitudes and persistent temporal correlations, supporting a phenomenological description involving multiplicative, temporally structures stochasticity. Polynomial and logistic-type drift functions are subsequently fitted to the deterministic components and integrated to reconstruct the epidemic incidence trajectories. Although polynomial drift provides high in-sample agreement with the deterministic dynamics, complexity-entropy analysis reveals that the reconstruction depends on the epidemic year and the embedding delay. A paired circular moving-block bootstrap further demonstrates that observed minimizing delays exhibit different levels of stability across the various reconstructions and years. Finally, we conducted a noise-amplitude sensitivity analysis, and it reveals pronounced changes in the optimal embedding delay and minimum Euclidean distance in the complexity-entropy plane. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach to characterizing structured stochastic fluctuations and assessing the temporal organization of epidemic dynamics.

authors.name: Athokpam Langlen Chanu
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On $p$-Adic Valuation Trees Arising from Laplace Transform of Fibonacci Polynomials
papers.abstract: We study the $p$-adic valuation trees associated with the sequence \[ e_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}F_n(t)\,dt, \] obtained by evaluating the Laplace transforms of the Fibonacci polynomials at $1$. We answer an open question of Givens and Moll in the negative by constructing an explicit counterexample showing that even internal branches need not be simple. We then reformulate the Givens--Moll lifting criteria for the even and odd subsequences in terms of the roots and derivatives of two associated polynomials. In particular, simple roots modulo $p$ give rise to simple internal branches. Finally, we develop a recursive lifting procedure that determines the unique surviving residue class at each level of a branch associated with a simple root and computes the $p$-adic valuations of the corresponding terms.

papers.title: A convexity theorem for proper Dupin hypersurfaces in spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a (compact, connected, and embedded) proper Dupin hypersurface in a sphere then, viewing $M$ as a submanifold of the ambient Euclidean space, its orthogonal projection to the normal space at any point is convex. This is a generalization of the convexity theorem of Terng for isoparametric submanifolds in Euclidean spaces.

papers.title: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths
papers.abstract: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL) attacks make the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent for email. This paper presents a systematic measurement that jointly examines PQC deployment across email service stages, negotiation by communicating peers, and usable message encryption. Endpoint-level support alone does not establish PQC readiness across email workflows because submission, relay, and access use independently negotiated Transport Layer Security (TLS) connections. We therefore combine three snapshots of relay, submission, access, and webmail services associated with the Tranco Top~1M domains with controlled tests of mail clients, sending servers, and OpenPGP and S/MIME implementations. Our measurements reveal a transition concentrated among a few providers, with available capability not consistently translating into actual use. Fewer than half of the domains in each service panel support PQC, and Google alone accounts for approximately 87\% of hybrid-capable relay domains. Only two of eight tested sending providers negotiate PQC with our receiver, although five accept it inbound. When TLS groups are restricted to PQC, four of the six incompatible senders fall back to plaintext where unencrypted SMTP remains permitted. At the message layer, limited native key generation, key-format incompatibilities, and backend integration failures further constrain usable PQC encryption.

authors.name: Jaehwan Park
authors.institution: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spatial Colorimetric Mapping of pH and Dissolved Carbon during Convective Dissolution of CO{\_2}: Constraints from Domain, Geometry, and Indicator Mix on Measurement Reliability
papers.abstract: Quantifying the dissolution and buoyancy-driven transport of CO2-rich water is critical to understanding solubility trapping mechanism in geologic storage. Analog-fluid density driven convection experiments do not represent CO2 dissolution chemistry or the aqueous CO2 density-concentration monotonic relationship. X-ray tomography does not provide enough contrast to directly measure dissolved CO2. Spatial colorimetry provides an inexpensive method to map pH and estimate total dissolved inorganic carbon (CT) via carbonate equilibrium assumptions. However, the effects of experimental conditions such as domain (free fluid and porous), geometry (2D and 3D), and indicator mix concentration on the reliability of pH and CT measurements remain unexplored. We evaluated how these factors affect the reliability of measurements using two different colorimetric models (hue and spherical coordinates ({\theta} and {\phi})). Hue was reliable in all domains whereas {\theta}-{\phi} was reliable in free fluid. Lower indicator mix concentration increased the chromatic sensitivity at low pH in free fluid; however, it did not produce sufficient color contrast for pH calibration and mapping in the porous domain. In the porous domain, {\theta}-{\phi} calibration was 33 times more susceptible to noise than hue. Temporal pH noise was less than 0.01 units; spatial noise changed domain-mean CT by 0.6-4.4{\%}. Both models were able to resolve CO2-rich plumes in free fluid; however, {\theta}-{\phi} had sharper plume boundaries than hue. The temporal evolution of CO2 dissolution resolved by the color models agreed more in 2D than 3D. These findings provide a reliability framework for studying subsurface dissolution and mixing of CO2.

papers.title: First-principles-based search for emergent topological spin textures in transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers
papers.abstract: Topological spin textures such as skyrmions and bimerons offer rich physical functionalities and strong potential for future spin-based technologies. Identifying materials that host such emergent magnetic states, however, remains challenging due to the complex interplay between microscopic magnetic interactions and large-scale spin textures. Here, using a multiscale first-principles discovery framework, we identify a broad class of two-dimensional materials that stabilize nontrivial spin textures. The framework integrates relativistic density functional theory, magnetic force theory, and atomistic spin-dynamics simulations, enabling a direct connection between electronic interactions and emergent magnetic textures and allowing efficient screening of systems with large magnetic unit cells and competing exchange interactions. Applying this approach, we systematically screen 312 monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides across 1T and 2H phases of 3d, 4d, and 5d transition metals. We uncover a diverse set of emergent spin textures, including skyrmions, bimerons, and complex domain states, and clarify their distinct stabilization mechanisms driven by exchange interactions, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, and magnetic frustration. These results identify promising candidate materials for topological spin textures and establish a transferable computational framework for accelerating materials discovery of complex magnetic states in two dimensions.

authors.name: Myung Joon Han
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: RadarCom: Unlocking Simultaneous Communication and Sensing on Commodity Automotive mmWave Radars
papers.abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication can improve road safety and traffic efficiency, yet its deployment remains limited by the need for dedicated communication hardware and supporting infrastructure. Meanwhile, production vehicles are already widely equipped with millimeter-wave radars for sensing. To unlock their communication potential, this paper presents RadarCom, a software-defined system that enables direct radar-to-radar communication on unmodified commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) automotive mmWave radars while preserving their native sensing functionality. The key insight is that mutual inter-radar interference, traditionally viewed as harmful, can be repurposed as a communication carrier. Based on this insight, RadarCom introduces slope-mismatch-based discovery, adaptive chirp synchronization, differential coding on range-FFT, and sensing-aware interference suppression to enable simultaneous communication and sensing without hardware modification, waveform redesign, or infrastructure support. We implement RadarCom on TI AWR2243 automotive radars and evaluate it under static, dynamic, and challenging real-world conditions. Results show an average effective data rate of 5.55 kbps with symbol error rates below 1.5%, while maintaining sensing F1 scores of up to 80.5% during concurrent communication. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transforming commodity automotive radars into dual-purpose communication and sensing devices.

authors.name: Yi Wei
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching: A Generative AI Framework for Global Total Electron Content Forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of global total electron content (TEC) is important for space weather monitoring and the reliable operation of satellite communication and navigation systems. We propose a physics-guided generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework for day-ahead global TEC forecasting. The framework builds on flow matching, which learns to gradually transform samples from an initial distribution into new samples that share the statistical characteristics of the target data. The proposed model incorporates ionospheric dynamics described by a partial differential equation (PDE) into this transformation process, guiding the changes between initial and target samples using physical knowledge. The model further combines the physical dynamics with statistical patterns captured from data to learn this transformation, adaptively adjusting their relative contributions at each location. The model is trained and evaluated using one year of global TEC data generated by the Thermosphere Ionosphere Electrodynamics General Circulation Model (TIEGCM). The results demonstrate that our model improves both spatial and temporal forecasting accuracy over representative benchmarks, including statistical, deep learning, and generative AI methods at all lead times and across latitudes. The average root mean square error (RMSE) is 39.2% lower than that of ConvLSTM and 23.8% lower than that of the same framework without physical guidance. The learned contribution weights vary systematically with latitude and across geographic locations, showing how the physical contribution changes across the forecast domain. These findings demonstrate that explicit physical guidance improves generative forecasts of global TEC and highlight the value of incorporating physical dynamics into generative AI modeling.

papers.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
papers.abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the H\"older Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each H\"older semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the H\"older Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the H\"older semicomplexes that can be realized as a H\"older Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.

papers.title: A Lightweight Dual-Branch Visual Front-End for Efficient Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction
papers.abstract: Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction (AVTSE) uses face-related visual cues to extract a target speaker from a speech mixture. In many AVTSE systems, visual features are obtained from convolutional image encoders, and their computation may become a non-negligible part of the overall system when lightweight separation backbones are used. This work proposes a dual-branch visual front-end that reorganizes visual information according to its spatial characteristics. A compact lip region of interest is used to model local articulation cues through convolutional processing, while facial landmark coordinates are used to represent global geometric motion with a lightweight temporal convolutional network. The two representations are integrated into IIANet and SpatialNet with limited fusion overhead. Experiments on LRS3-2mix under a unified reduced training protocol show that the proposed method achieves a performance-computation trade-off close to the lightweight image-based baseline. Compared with the ResNet18-based visual encoder, it reduces the module-level visual encoding computation by more than 90% across both evaluated separation backbones, with a moderate performance gap. This comparison excludes face detection and landmark estimation and therefore applies to systems where landmark coordinates are already available from preprocessing. Demos are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Lightweight-Visual-Frontend-E46E.

papers.title: Improving Learned AC-OPF Feasibility under Distribution Shift with PF-in-the-Loop Correction
papers.abstract: Learning-based AC-OPF enables fast dispatch, yet its feasibility can degrade under distribution shift. We analyze three state-of-the-art methods and identify a shared deployment-time limitation: none use feedback from the power-flow (PF)-realized state to ensure feasibility of the predicted control. Using a simple PF-in-the-loop feasibility restoration filter, we empirically show that such feedback substantially improves hard feasibility across four out-of-distribution scenarios with modest runtime overhead.

papers.title: LM-DSB: A Lightweight Multi-agent System for Automated Daily Safety Bulletin Generation in Construction
papers.abstract: Construction safety management still struggles to produce daily safety bulletins (DSBs), structured daily communications that identify site-specific hazards, convey safety protocols, and set preventive measures for workers. Manual DSB creation takes 2-3 hours daily and yields inconsistent quality, with 25% of crews never conducting pretask planning (Olson et al., 2016), diverting safety personnel from field supervision. This study proposes the Lightweight Multi-Agent DSB System (LM-DSB), which integrates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a locally deployable Large Language Model (LLM) to automate DSB generation on consumer-grade personal computers. LM-DSB coordinates specialized planner, researcher, and writer agents in a hierarchical architecture, enhanced by domain-specific fine-tuning on construction safety documentation and RAG grounding in 37 health, safety, and environment (HSE) documents. A two-phase validation assessed feasibility. Phase 1 comparative evaluation showed the multi-agent RAG system (Llama 3-8B) outperformed all alternative configurations, with strong lexical alignment and coherence (TF-IDF: 0.70, BLEU: 0.39, ROUGE-1: 0.66) and near-complete document generation (length ratio: 1.01 vs. 0.39 for single-agent RAG). Phase 2 expert evaluation (N=40) confirmed practical acceptability (mean scores 3.50-4.20 on a 5-point scale), particularly in regulatory compliance (4.20) and factual accuracy (4.10). The findings show that architectural design enables lightweight models to handle safety-critical documentation on consumer-grade hardware, advancing technology democratization in construction safety management. Limitations include knowledge base scope, language constraints, and lack of field deployment validation; future work should address multimodal integration and workflow adoption.

papers.title: semanticfa: An R Package for Response-Free Semantic Factor Analysis of Psychometric Scales
papers.abstract: The items of a reflective psychometric scale can be read as a proposal about a construct's structure. Language models make that proposal measurable by converting each item into an embedding, a list of numbers, similar for similar meanings. We introduce semanticfa, an R package for semantic factor analysis, which factors item-embedding similarities. It also interprets factors, flags redundant items, builds short forms, and screens new items. A worked example analyzes the 50-item International Personality Item Pool Big-Five Factor Markers, embedded with Qwen3-Embedding-8B, and compares the results with a factor analysis of 874,434 respondents. Retention criteria tied between five and six factors, and the tie rule kept five. Three corresponded mainly to single domains, and two blended most Extraversion items with five Agreeableness items. Each factor's congruence with its best-matching human factor (1 = identical) ranged from .92 for Openness to .52 for Agreeableness. Item pairs more similar in meaning tended to be answered more alike (r = .46 with raw responses), but same-domain reverse-keyed opposites, answered oppositely, were about as similar as cross-domain pairs (.58 vs. .57). Sign-flipping reverse-keyed items' embeddings did not improve agreement with raw responses and worsened it with reverse-scored ones. With five factors, a 25-item short form matched the domains better than all 200 random five-per-domain sets, but parallel analysis kept only three. We propose semantic-behavioral coherence, the agreement between semantic and response structures, as a measurable property of a scale, given an embedding model. Semantic factor analysis complements, and does not replace, response-based factor analysis.

papers.title: Rotational Perturbation Theory for Magnetic Interactions
papers.abstract: We develop rotational perturbation theory for magnetic interactions in collinear and noncollinear systems, distinguishing prescribed rotations of exchange fields from constrained rotations of magnetic moments. At the full exchange splitting, we derive Green-function expressions for prescribedfield energy curvatures directly from perturbation theory, without invoking the local force theorem; constrained-moment curvatures additionally require the stationary magnetic response and are related to the inverse static susceptibility. We examine noncollinear pair interactions and planar and conical spin spirals, and derive the long-wavelength ferromagnetic spin-wave stiffness and, assuming adiabatic sublattice precession, the antiferromagnetic spin-wave velocity. Orbital-nonlocal magnetic potentials and correlated electronic response reveal further requirements for connecting rotational curvatures to collective magnetic behavior. As a practical extension, we project the complete transverse pair Hessian onto an effective scalar Heisenberg exchange and quantify the unreconstructed curvature. Biquadratic and three-spin examples illustrate why locally extracted exchange coefficients need not represent transferable bilinear interactions.

papers.title: Bayesian Treed Vecchia Gaussian Process Emulation via Sequential Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Computer models (or simulators) are used in many scientific domains to understand and predict real-world processes, but they are expensive to run. One way to address this hurdle is to use Gaussian processes (GPs). For complex physical systems such as storm surge, simulator outputs often exhibit heterogeneous structures, and many nonstationary GP methods become impractical with several inputs and tens of thousands of runs. To address these issues, we combine the divide-and-conquer idea of treed GP models with Vecchia approximations in a Bayesian treed Vecchia GP (TVGP) model. The model uses the Bayesian classification and regression tree prior for random recursive partitioning of the input domain. Within each leaf, a Vecchia approximation allows efficient likelihood evaluation. For Bayesian inference, we develop a sequential Monte Carlo algorithm that explores tree space as an alternative to reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo. The method is demonstrated on synthetic examples with two and ten inputs and on a storm-surge simulator with seven inputs and up to 50,649 training runs. TVGP has the smallest prediction error in both synthetic examples and with the larger storm-surge training set, although its predictive intervals undercover in the example with ten inputs and the storm-surge application.

authors.name: Cong Ye
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Refractories and Metallurgy

papers.title: How Stable Are LLM-Generated Proofs Under Program Refactoring? A Stress Test for Verifiable Code Generation
papers.abstract: Benchmarks for verifiable code generation usually test a proof against one fixed implementation. We ask whether the same proof remains valid after a program refactoring that preserves behavior. We introduce RefactorProof, which derives 458 Lean-certified variants from the 185 VERINA tasks that compile in our pinned environment while holding the specification and evaluated proof fixed byte-for-byte. VERINA supplies reference proofs for 46 tasks, all from its basic split; the primary model-versus-reference comparisons further match on 21-25 short, non-recursive tasks. Structural refactorings expose substantial brittleness across proof sources: task-normalized structural PSR is 4.3% for the supplied references and 13.3-26.8% for the specialized provers. On the matched tasks, specialized prover proofs nevertheless have higher overall unchanged-proof survival than the supplied reference artifacts: +15.6 points for DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, +18.8 for Goedel-Prover-V2-32B, and +20.3 for Goedel-Prover-V2-8B; all three 95% CIs exclude zero. The ordering persists after excluding universally survived T1 variants, under family-balanced aggregation, and under alternative deployable valid-proof selection rules. However, unchanged-proof failure is not the same as high repair cost: predefined one-identifier edits repair 51/54 eligible reference structural failures and 58/85 eligible prover failures. RefactorProof therefore measures unchanged-proof stability under program refactoring, not the cost of maintaining a proof after it breaks.

papers.title: Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$
papers.abstract: We report electrical tuning of spin relaxation in atomically thin $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, a representative low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide. Weak antilocalization measurements reveal strong spin--orbit interaction with spin--orbit lengths of tens of nanometers, consistent with recent theoretical predictions. Despite the semimetallic nature of $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, in the ultrathin limit the spin--orbit scattering time can be tuned electrostatically by up to threefold. We further investigate vertical electric field effects on the spin--orbit length and time, and demonstrate the modulation of the Rashba parameters. Relation between spin--orbit scattering time and the diffusion coefficient indicates that spin relaxation is governed by the D'yakonov--Perel' mechanism in both monolayer and bilayer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$. These results establish few-layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$ as a platform for electrically tunable spin transport, thereby providing insight into spin relaxation in low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenides.

papers.title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
papers.abstract: Opening a band gap in metallic two-dimensional carbon allotropes is an important step toward their use in electronic and optoelectronic devices, and full hydrogenation has proven to be an effective route to achieve it. Here, we propose irida-graphane, the fully hydrogenated derivative of the irida-graphene, a monolayer composed of three-, six-, and eight-membered rings, and investigate its structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties using density functional theory (DFT) at the PBE and HSE06 levels combined with phonon and \textit{ab initio} molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. All carbon atoms adopt $sp^3$ hybridization, with the hydrogen atoms of the three- and six-membered rings bonded to opposite sides of a buckled carbon framework, and the lattice parameter contracts by 4.3% with respect to irida-graphene. The hydrogenation energy of $-0.53$ eV/H indicates that the hydrogenation of irida-graphene from molecular hydrogen is exothermic. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies confirms the dynamical stability of irida-graphane, and AIMD simulations show that its structure remains intact at temperatures up to 2000 K. Irida-graphane is mechanically isotropic, with an in-plane stiffness of approximately 156 N/m, a Poisson's ratio of approximately 0.1, and critical strains of approximately 20%. Hydrogenation transforms the metallic parent structure into a semiconductor with an indirect band gap of 4.68 eV (PBE) and 6.0 eV (HSE06). Irida-graphane is transparent in the visible range, with reflectivity below 0.3%, and absorbs strongly in the deep ultraviolet, with absorption coefficients of the order of $10^{5} - 10^{6}$ cm$^{-1}$. These results suggest irida-graphane as a candidate wide-gap material for ultraviolet optoelectronics and transparent coatings.

papers.title: New upper bounds for average kissing numbers
papers.abstract: A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors. For a finite packing of balls, its average contact number is the average number of balls tangent to a ball in this packing, that is, twice the total number of tangencies divided by the number of balls. The average kissing number of the space is defined as the supremum of average contact numbers over all finite ball packings. In this paper, we present a new semidefinite programming approach to average kissing numbers and improve upon known upper bounds in all dimensions \(3\) through \(30\). In particular, we provide the first improvements to the upper bounds in dimensions \(10\) through \(30\) obtained from kissing numbers. We also fully solve the average kissing number problem in dimensions \(8\) and \(24\) by showing that the average kissing numbers coincide with the kissing numbers, 240 and 196560, respectively. These values are limits of average contact numbers of finite subpackings from the \(E_8\) and Leech lattices.

papers.title: Taming Multi-Dimensional Skew in Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Contention-Aware Scheduling [Technical Report]
papers.abstract:
Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is a key kernel in graph analytics, relational queries, and machine learning. Yet, its performance remains a significant challenge, due to the inherent sparsity and, more critically, the prevalent skew patterns often found in real-world workloads. This paper investigates this problem and demonstrates that an unbalanced workload distribution is the main culprit, harming performance through two co-existing root causes: first, multi-dimensional skew, where imbalance across computation cost, output density, and data locality cannot be captured by any single balancing metric; and second, cache contention, where dense substructures induce severe on-chip interference.
  To that end, we propose adaptive morsel scheduling (AMS), a dynamic scheduling framework that decouples skew dimensions via fixed-result-size morsels and integrates contention-aware load balancing (CALB) and data-conscious simultaneous multithreading activator (SMTact) to alleviate cache-level contention, alongside a hybrid accumulation mechanism (HYB) that adaptively selects the best accumulator per morsel. Evaluations across matrix squaring, relational queries, graph analytics, and other sparse matrix kernels show that AMS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on skewed workloads while maintaining comparable performance on non-skewed ones. These gains, along with improved bandwidth utilization, remain valid across a wide range of workloads and hardware systems.

papers.title: Live-OPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Proactive Streaming Large Video Models
papers.abstract: Streaming multimodal assistants must make response decisions while events are still unfolding. They need to recognize when the available evidence warrants a response, produce an appropriate continuation, and remain silent otherwise. Supervised fine-tuning learns from recorded assistant turns, but does not directly train on the response prefixes produced by the evolving policy itself. We introduce Live-OPSD, an on-policy self-distillation method that uses privileged hints available only during training to supervise the policy on its own outputs. The policy first generates a continuation from the streaming context alone. The same model then re-evaluates that continuation with a hint describing the relevant evidence, and the resulting distributions guide the unhinted policy. On Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B, Live-OPSD attains an average score of 59.64 on LiveProBench, 5.26 points above the strongest continued-SFT baseline, and stays competitive on OVO-Bench (65.84). These results indicate that guiding the policy on its own outputs with privileged hints improves both when and how a streaming assistant responds.

papers.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
papers.abstract: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs. However, effective program search requires physical understanding: agents must understand how objects can be manipulated, how scene geometry constrains actions, and why interactions succeed or fail. Existing methods rely mainly on execution feedback for program refinement, often leaving these physical questions unresolved. We introduce RoboAuto, a framework for robot program search that explicitly organizes physical understanding at the object, scene, and interaction levels through three components. First, a hierarchical knowledge base combines executable skills with object-centric knowledge of affordances, spatial relations, and action effects, learned from embodied data and online task solving. Second, scene grounding connects this knowledge to the current environment by identifying relevant objects and resolving action-critical quantities. Third, multi-stage planning with self-designed experiments checks whether each stage produces its expected physical effects and actively tests competing hypotheses to resolve physical uncertainties. RoboAuto achieves superior performance across five benchmark families, attaining an 89.1% success rate on short-horizon LIBERO-PRO tasks and more than twice the mean success rate of ASPIRE on LIBERO-PRO Long and LIBERO-Plus. It also outperforms ASPIRE and $\pi_{0.5}$ on three challenging long-horizon real-robot tasks requiring precise manipulation. We further show that the knowledge base transfers across simulators and embodiments, and that program search performance scales with its size. Project page: https://roboauto-ai.github.io/

papers.title: Multireference Second-Order Perturbation Theories Based on Iterative Configuration Interaction with Selection
papers.abstract: Under the assumption that the static correlation can well be described by selected configuration interaction, to the extent that the residual dynamic correlation can be accounted for accurately by a second-order perturbation theory (PT2), a family of multireference PT2s (iCI-MRPT2) based on the iterative configuration interaction with selection are proposed and compared. The first step is to partition a large complete active space (CAS) $P$ into the direct sum of a primary ($P_m$) and a secondary ($P_s$) subspace via a parameter $C_{\mathrm{min}}$. The former serves as the actual reference space, whereas the latter is treated via Epstein-Nesbet PT2. An MRPT2 is then invoked to account for the dynamic correction of the $Q=1-P$ space to the $P_m$ space. Different MRPT2s are distinguished by the underlying zeroth-order Hamiltonians. To circumvent the prohibitive computational cost and memory footprint associated with high-order reduced density matrices in the fully internally contracted scheme and the exponential growth of external functions (XF) in the uncontracted scheme, a partial contraction strategy is employed for constructing the XFs: those involving one or two inactive (core or virtual) orbitals are kept uncontracted, whereas those involving three or four inactive orbitals are internally contracted. They span the uncontracted ($Q_u$) and contracted ($Q_c$) portions of $Q$, respectively. The former is further split into two subspaces $Q_u^c$ and $Q_u^u$ via a parameter $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$, which are to be treated in coupled and uncoupled manners, respectively. Extrapolations to zero $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{min}}$ can be performed, so as to approach CAS-based MRPT2. Calculations with active spaces as large as CAS(56e,58o) can now be performed. The size-consistency of the iCI-MRPT2s is also analyzed in detail.

papers.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

papers.title: Decoupling Consistency and Conflict across MLLM Layers for Fake News Detection
papers.abstract: The trustworthiness of Web content faces a growing threat from multimodal fake news. Real news usually shows aligned image-text semantics, while fake news often contains a few conflicts at varying levels, such as mismatches in objects, scenes, events, and claims. However, existing methods usually treat consistency and conflict in a coarse and static way, limiting their ability to capture sparse conflicts and adapt to varying conflict levels. Inspired by the distinct knowledge encoded across layers in large language models, we propose Multi-Level Consistency and Conflict Decoupling (MLCCD), which captures conflicts at different levels from different layers of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Specifically, we first use the MLLM's final decision representation to select visual and textual tokens relevant to the task, preventing irrelevant content from diluting sparse conflicts. Then, we preserve tokens whose representations change sharply between adjacent layers, capturing the knowledge each layer adds. Finally, we decouple this knowledge into consistency and conflict evidence and aggregate each across layers with its own router, adapting to varying conflict levels. Experiments on three benchmarks show that MLCCD outperforms existing methods.

papers.title: Spectral Braids: A Topological Descriptor for Dynamic Directed Networks
papers.abstract: Eigenvalues are a workhorse of graph machine learning: spectral clustering, spectral graph neural networks, and graph kernels all summarize a network by the eigenvalues of a matrix. These eigenvalues are almost always treated as a static list of numbers. When a graph changes, however, its eigenvalues move, and when the matrix is not symmetric, they move in the complex plane, where they can wind around each other. The pattern of this winding is a braid, a classical object from topology. We propose spectral braids, a methodology for dynamic directed networks: each snapshot is aggregated into a community-level transition matrix, its complex eigenvalues are tracked over time, and the braid they trace is read off as a word. The word is then mapped to a matrix by the Burau representation, which gives a fixed-size feature vector for any classifier. The braid has a concrete meaning: each eigenvalue describes how a group of communities behaves, and each crossing records one group overtaking another. We evaluate the method on dynamic network classification, using synthetic networks of online communities whose labels describe how the network evolved between the same starting and ending states. Our experimental results show that the proposed features reach 97.1% accuracy on four classes, against 44.5% for the best feature set that does not track eigenvalues, and that the Burau features also separate networks containing the same events in a different order, which simple counts of crossings cannot do. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that defines braids and braid monodromy on graph data and uses them as features for learning on dynamic networks.

papers.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
papers.abstract: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology. Supervised graph-based models achieve strong performance, but are often trained for a particular dataset and sensor graph, making deployment to new or evolving networks costly. Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) offer a zero-shot alternative by learning in-context inference from synthetic task priors, which provide an explicit mechanism for encoding domain-specific assumptions. Existing forecasting PFNs, however, do not explicitly represent the graph-structured dependencies governing traffic dynamics. To combine graph-aware traffic modeling with zero-shot adaptation, we introduce the Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Network (GAS-PFN). GAS-PFN incorporates sampled road topology into its synthetic task prior through random-walk diffusion, teaching the model to learn graph-coupled dynamics during pretraining. Its co-designed inference architecture uses two mask-conditioned passes through a shared Transformer backbone to separately model sensor-specific temporal dynamics and spatiotemporal interactions among neighboring sensors before integrating their representations for prediction. This design enables GAS-PFN to use target-network structure and context without parameter updates. Across six benchmarks at the 90-minute horizon, GAS-PFN reduces MSE by 34.0% on average relative to TimePFN, its closest PFN-based predecessor. It also reduces MSE by 27.7% on average relative to four recent industry-developed general-purpose zero-shot forecasters. In this comparison, all models receive 90 minutes of contiguous recent history, and any additional context is drawn from each dataset's chronological training split. These results indicate that aligning PFN priors and inference architectures with graph structure improves in-context learning for zero-shot traffic forecasting.

authors.name: Yifan Zhang

papers.title: RouteDRAG: Learning to Route and Control Agentic Execution for Multimodal Document RAG
papers.abstract: Web-based applications increasingly rely on understanding long multimodal documents, where answering questions often requires combining information across pages, tables, and figures. Agentic retrieval-augmented generation addresses these tasks through iterative retrieval and reasoning. However, Agentic execution is not always necessary, introducing additional computation and potentially incorrect answers. Our empirical analysis reveals that Agentic execution provides query-dependent benefits, while additional operations may improve, preserve, or degrade answer accuracy. These findings motivate controlling both Agent invocation and subsequent execution. To address these challenges, we propose RouteDRAG, a learning-based framework comprising four components. Unified Document Index organizes multimodal content into a graph-backed index and derives query representations from initial retrieval. Adaptive Path Routing preserves exact answering and predicts the relative benefit of Agent over shorter execution paths. Dynamic Agent Execution maintains an evolving workspace and refines Planner proposals to control tool use and termination. Sequential Policy Learning first trains operation control from observed outcomes and then trains path routing using the resulting Agent's performance. Across two benchmarks, RouteDRAG achieves an average accuracy improvement of 3.47 percentage points over shorter-path-only execution while assigning only 79.3% of queries to Agent. Notably, it also surpasses uniform Agent execution on both benchmarks while requiring fewer answering calls. Our code is now available at https://github.com/Ereshkigal1/RouteDRAG.

papers.title: LearnPrunerV2: Learnable Progressive Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable multimodal capabilities but suffer from prohibitive computational overhead due to the massive number of visual tokens. While token pruning is a promising solution, existing methods still suffer from two major drawbacks: 1) unreliable pruning criteria that fail to accurately localize task-specific regions due to inherent attention biases or query-agnostic designs, and 2) suboptimal pruning strategies that employ rigid, non-adaptive schedules, overlooking the dynamic evolution of token redundancy across different model depths. To address these challenges, we propose LearnPrunerV2, which extends the previous two-stage heuristic framework (LearnPruner) into a fully learnable architecture. Specifically, we integrate lightweight learnable modules into every layer of the VLM backbone, which estimate token importance by fusing intrinsic visual saliency with extrinsic query relevance captured via a shadow token. By uncovering a consistent staircase redundancy pattern across VLM layers, we further introduce Budget-Deterministic Pruning (BDP) to establish a hardware-friendly schedule with fixed per-layer budgets. Extensive experimental results across various benchmarks and VLMs demonstrate that LearnPrunerV2 consistently outperform previous state-of-the-art methods. Notably, LearnPrunerV2 preserves 99.8% of the original performance when pruning 77.8% of visual tokens on LLaVA-v1.5, achieving a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

papers.title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for breast imaging, but limited labeled data, institutional data fragmentation, and privacy concerns hinder centralized training. We investigate a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with client-level differential privacy. We compare general-purpose CLIP models, biomedical BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 baseline on two public breast imaging datasets, with and without differential privacy. We also evaluate a CLIP ViT-B/16 ablation that removes the text pathway. Evaluation includes patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, baseline comparisons, threshold sensitivity, inter-model agreement, and communication cost. Under federated learning, all five models achieve high normal-versus-sick discrimination (ROC-AUC: 0.940-0.990). However, acquisition year alone achieves 0.974 on the same test partition, raising concerns about confounding rather than genuine pathology recognition. Benign-versus-malignant discrimination remains uncertain (ROC-AUC: 0.504-0.637), with all confidence intervals including 0.50. Removing the text pathway preserves classification accuracy while halving communication cost. Differential privacy reduces ROC-AUC by 0.375, attributable to perturbing the full model state rather than only trainable parameters. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating confounding, predictive reliability, privacy implementation, and deployment efficiency when developing federated AI systems for breast imaging.

authors.name: Md Zobaer Islam

papers.title: Multidimensional Infinite-Horizon Markovian Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Continuous Coefficients and Nonzero-Sum Differential Games
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the solvability of multidimensional infinite-horizon Markovian backward stochastic differential equations with continuous coefficients. We do not require the Lipschitz property or other quantitative controls of differences, and each component of the generator is allowed to depend simultaneously on all components of the multidimensional backward variables. A local L^q-domination framework adapted to the infinite-horizon setting is developed and combined with our linear flow conjugacy analysis to obtain the required distributional control in the presence of unbounded linear drift. We also derive a common Markov representation valid for the entire family of initial states. The analytical obstacles arising from weak regularity and the multidimensional structure are thereby overcome. Furthermore, we consider a class of infinite-horizon nonzero-sum differential games with a general non linear structure, allowing player controls to be fully coupled and permitting payoff criteria that are not restricted to an exponential discount form, establish an equivalence between the game and the corresponding multidimensional infinite-horizon backward stochastic differential equations, and prove the existence of a Nash equilibrium.

authors.name: Zhen Wu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in $H^{1/2}_\bullet$
papers.abstract:
We prove sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation on the real line $\R$ in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). This regularity threshold for global well-posedness is optimal, as we show by constructing examples of ill-posedness in \(H^s_\bullet\) for any \(s<1/2\). Moreover, with the spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of initial data in the energy space, we prove that solutions in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\) asymptotically decouple as an infinite superposition of solitons. Our results extend the known global well-posedness and finite soliton resolution for rational data in \(H^\infty_\bullet\) to sharp global well-posedness and soliton resolution for general data in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\).
  Different from rational solutions, general data can also involve an infinite discrete spectrum, which makes the reduction analysis framework on the finite rank no longer applicable. For sharp well-posedness, we present a new isometry criterion and stability results for resolvent transform in the explicit formula. For soliton resolution, we develop a spectral method for this equation based on direct resolvent analysis and a novel trace norm estimate that upgrades energy convergence to uniform convergence. Our argument also yields sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the generalized half-wave maps equation with targets in the complex Grassmannians, extending the classical sphere-valued case.

authors.name: Fei Tang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: PsyJev: Psychological Analysis via System-1 Judgment
papers.abstract: Self-disclosures on the Web support diverse psychological analyses, from recognizing expressed experiences to identifying symptom-relevant information. We study a shared, question-conditioned decision interface for this heterogeneous problem in content analysis. We organize PsyJudgeBench, comprising 13 annotated datasets and 82 questions across six psychological areas, while preserving source-specific criteria and masks for unobserved labels. We introduce PsyJev, a System-1 model that directly produces distributions over answers specified in each request. Joint supervised training establishes the shared judgment function, followed by Judgment-Anchored RLCD (JA-RLCD), which adapts logit-space reward optimization to heterogeneous psychological judgments through balanced supervision, selective retention of correct SFT predictions, and question-group reward optimization. The Qwen3.5-based 2B, 4B, and 9B models achieve 64.33, 66.21, and 67.56 average test F1, respectively. The 9B model exceeds the strongest external comparison by 2.54 points. Controlled 2B comparisons examine the training stages and anchored refinement. Further analyses examine question-conditioned judgment, inference cost, and probability quality, complemented by qualitative comparisons across models.

papers.title: Resolving a Problem of Lv and Koolen on the Smallest Eigenvalue of Distance-Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D\ge3$, and eigenvalues $k=\theta_0>\theta_1>\cdots>\theta_D$. Put $b\coloneqq b_1/(\theta_1+1)$, and let $1=u_0>u_1>\cdots>u_D$ be the standard sequence associated with $\theta_1$. Lv and Koolen asked whether the negative of the smallest eigenvalue of a distance-regular graph can be bounded above in terms of its diameter $D$ and the parameter $b$ alone. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proving that $-\theta_D\le\prod_{i=2}^D(1-u_i)/(u_1-u_i) <(b+1)^{D-1}$. Equality in the product bound holds if and only if $\Gamma$ is $Q$-polynomial with respect to the primitive idempotent corresponding to $\theta_1$. For every integer $D\ge4$, we further establish the explicit bound $-\theta_D\le b^{D-1}+b^{D-2} +\frac{27}{2}(D-2)b^{D-3}$ whenever $b\ge\max\{8,\sqrt{12(D-2)}\}$. Both leading coefficients are best possible for each fixed $D\ge4$. The proof uses a spectral product theorem of Micchelli and Willoughby applied to Schur multiplication in the Bose--Mesner algebra.

authors.name: Zhen-Mu Hong
authors.institution: Anhui University of Finance and Economics

papers.title: Irreducibility Testing of Sparse Polynomials over Integers is NP-hard and Probabilistic Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that irreducibility testing for sparse polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ is coNP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. That is, there exists no polynomial-time irreducibility test algorithm unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$. We also provide an upper bound for this problem by demonstrating that the same irreducibility testing problem lies in $\mathsf{PP}\subseteq\mathsf{PSPACE}$; in other words, it can be solved in probabilistic polynomial time and, moreover, within polynomial space. The fact that $\mathsf{SparseIrred}_{\mathbb{Z}}\in\mathsf{PP}$ relies on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis result of Cureton--Thorner and on the uniform effective prime-ideal bound by Frei--Sofos--Widmer just posted recently.

papers.title: Spectral Oscillations and Temporal Meandering of Dissipative Solitons in a Moving Intracavity Phase Potential
papers.abstract: Dissipative solitons (DSs) provide a prototypical platform for studying nonequilibrium dynamics governed by the interplay between nonlinearity, dissipation, and external driving. In particular, subjected to external potentials, DSs exhibit a rich variety of nonlinear dynamical behaviors. This work investigates DS dynamics in a moving intracavity potential generated by phase modulation whose frequency is detuned from an integer multiple of the cavity repetition rate. Modulation detuning introduces a timescale mismatch between the DS and the moving potential, leading to two distinct dynamical regimes. At large detuning, the DS cannot continuously track the moving potential and exhibits persistent spectral oscillations and temporal meandering, whereas at sufficiently small detuning it enters a synchronized locking state. Furthermore, both the oscillation period and amplitude can be tuned via the modulation detuning and modulation depth. These results reveal how asynchronous driving reshapes DS dynamics and establish a route for controlling their dynamical response in nonlinear optical cavities.

papers.title: Spatial MIMO Channel Rendering: A 3D Gaussian Splatting Approach
papers.abstract: The achievable gains of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems depend on channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition consumes pilot and feedback resources for every user in every coherence interval. Meanwhile, the propagation environment that shapes the channel persists. Exploiting such information will help to greatly reduce the overhead of CSI acquisition. This paper investigates the spatial MIMO channel rendering problem, which learns a latent beamspace channel scene from sparse observations and renders the long-term transmit and receive beam pair power map at unobserved user locations. Motivated by 3D Gaussian splatting in visual scene rendering, the proposed MIMO Gaussian splatting (MIMO-GS) represents the scene with pairs of receive and transmit 3D Gaussians, projects them from the user and base station onto the corresponding beam domains, and accumulates the beam associations through beam pair splatting. On a simulated urban scenario and measured indoor channels, MIMO-GS renders 5.5 times faster than ray tracing without a calibrated replica. Applied to multiuser beam management, the rendered maps allow users and transmit beams to be scheduled without sounding while accounting for the inter-user interference, and the net sum rate reaches 98% of the genie-aided benchmark, 19% above a position-based predictor.

authors.name: Jeonghun Park
authors.institution: The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

papers.title: safeL4: Rethinking Safe-Language-Based Single Address Space Microkernels
papers.abstract: Microkernels provide good features such as high security, safety, and flexibility, but their reliance on hardware-based isolation leads to heavy performance overhead, limiting their widespread adoption. Although constructing single-address-space microkernels based on safe language-based isolation is a promising approach to addressing the performance issue, this approach still faces challenges in maintaining the principle of minimality and enforcing capability-based, fine-grained access control over system resources. We propose safeL4, an approach to constructing microkernels based on safe languages. It guarantees minimality through low-level abstractions for unsafe operations, and implements a capability system based on the safe language's object capabilities to achieve fine-grained access control over all operations on system resources. We implement a prototype system in Rust, and our evaluation results show that the primitives provided by safeL4 are, on average, 1.9$\times$ faster than those of seL4.

authors.name: Shijun Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
