authors.name: Hongxin Guo
authors.institution: Center for High Pressure Science & Technology Advanced Research

authors.name: Guozhi Lin
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: An Algebra of Transformers
papers.abstract: On the theoretic analyses on transforms, they mainly focus on the computability analysis, such the Turing-completeness of unbounded precision transformers, the advantage of parallelizability of unbounded precision transformers and the limitations of bounded precision transformers. This paper give transformers an algebra for reasoning, which relies heavily on the functional decomposition results of transformers. This algebra uses functional decompositions as atomic actions, includes sequential composition and parallel composition, recursion for feedback and abstraction for hidden layers. As we know, it is the first attempt to model transformers logically and can be used to verify the correctness of transformer based applications.

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

papers.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
papers.abstract: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

papers.title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.

papers.title: RELAY: One Query, Two Roles for Sequential Recommendation
papers.abstract: Sequential recommendation must combine semantic preferences with behavioral associations to deliver accurate rankings at low inference cost. Sharing history selection connects preference representation directly to the behavioral evidence used in candidate scoring. We present RELAY, a compact sequential recommender built around one query, two roles: semantic readout and behavioral-memory routing. A single learned query forms a semantic preference representation and reuses its attention to route direct-history and transition evidence into candidate scores. Candidate-conditioned gates calibrate the two memory channels for each candidate. RELAY trains both roles with a single catalog likelihood and produces the final ranking in one forward pass. Full-catalog experiments on six datasets show that RELAY achieves the highest Recall@5 and NDCG@5 among the compared methods on every dataset, improving over the previous best model by 14.22% and 17.88% on average. With 2.044 million predictor parameters, RELAY reduces predictor size by 65.12% and achieves a 1.75~1.79$\times$ inference speedup over the previous best model.

papers.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Bias in MLLM for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long-video question answering is challenging since the answer often hinges on a few decisive moments scattered throughout the video, while memory constraints force Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to sample frames at extremely low rates, resulting in sparsity that risks omitting key evidence. Though aggressively enlarging the context size is intuitive, we argue that performance remains fundamentally constrained by the bias, \emph{i.e.}, the misleading cues caused by spurious \textit{linguistic} correlations and salient yet irrelevant \textit{visual} observations. In this paper, we first introduce {S-MME}, a benchmark designed to systematically diagnose shortcut-biased behavior in MLLMs. To mitigate this failure, we further propose a training-free framework, Counterfactual Long-video Evidence-Aware Reasoning (CLEAR). By treating the full video-question pair as a complete view, CLEAR estimates bias effects via augmented views by only keeping the question or locally salient visual clips. Then, we intervene hidden states to mitigate the discrepancy at inference such that the correct answer can be predicted confidently. With experimental studies across five benchmarks, we show that our method is generalizable and can be integrated in different MLLMs, yielding consistent gains in prediction and robustness. We hope CLEAR can offer a complementary direction in test-time scaling for long-video understanding.

authors.name: Jiawei Ma
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ASPEN: Adaptive Semantic Reasoning via Command Persistence Prediction for Efficient Navigation VLAs
papers.abstract: Navigation vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke costly semantic reasoning even when the next command remains unchanged. Command reuse can reduce computation but risks missing instruction-dependent turns or stops. We introduce ASPEN, an event-triggered scheduler based on command persistence prediction: estimating whether the frozen base policy would reissue its previous command. A lightweight multimodal predictor combines temporal observations, language instructions, execution history, and cached VLA confidence. At eligible command boundaries, sufficient predicted persistence permits command reuse. Otherwise, ASPEN triggers fresh semantic reasoning from the VLA. Evaluated with frozen NaVILA on cross-dataset RxR-CE val-unseen, ASPEN reduces VLA calls by 9.5% and estimated inference time by 8.1%, including scheduling overhead. It maintains comparable navigation performance and preserves identical baseline action sequences on 92.1% of episodes.

papers.title: CrowdCC: Jointly Benchmarking Corruption Robustness and Deployment Quantization in Crowd Counting
papers.abstract: Crowd-counting models deployed on edge devices face two shifts: inputs are degraded along the capture and transmission pipeline, while models are quantized to satisfy resource constraints. Yet corruption robustness and deployment quantization are typically evaluated separately. We introduce CrowdCC, a controlled corruption benchmark that jointly evaluates these effects using 23 deployment-motivated corruptions at three severity levels, four crowd-counting datasets, and 26 models using A100 TensorRT engines at FP32, FP16, and post-training INT8 precision, paired with throughput and energy measurements from corresponding Jetson Orin NX configurations. The corruptions span six families, with head annotations adjusted when geometry or visibility changes. Our evaluation shows that capture-chain corruptions consistently produce the largest degradation across the evaluated models, while crowd density affects absolute and relative error differently. Clean accuracy does not fully predict corrupted performance. INT8 alters corruption robustness substantially more than FP16, with no systematic direction, and does not consistently improve latency or energy. INT8 inference efficiency is strongly associated with reformat overhead in the compiled engine, while slowdowns are also observed under limited INT8 coverage. Precision changes corrupted-error rankings and robustness-cost frontiers, showing why model selection must consider corruption robustness and measured deployment cost together. The code is available at https://github.com/Tulane-Computer-Architecture-Systems/CrowdCC-Release.

authors.name: Lu Peng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moir\'e Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
papers.abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moir\'e lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. Using this six-level modulation strategy, the fabricated GO Moir\'e lens achieves continuous focal-length tuning from approximately 10 to 90 mm. Full-colour imaging with magnifications ranging from 1X to 9X is experimentally demonstrated. These results establish a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy for efficient multilevel GO flat optics and demonstrate its potential for compact, reconfigurable imaging.

papers.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
papers.abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.

papers.title: A Topology-Aware Neural Network for Fault Location With Missing Measurements
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a topology-aware neural network-based fault locator (TANFL) for radial distribution feeders, which uses voltage and current phasors obtained after the decay of fault induced transients, as well as feeder connection relationships and line parameters, as inputs. The shared bus encoder, bus readout module, and gated line readout module work together to identify the faulty bus or line and estimate the continuous fault location on the selected line. During training, explicit missing data indicators and random bus data block masking are introduced, enabling a single trained model to handle both complete measurement sets and scenarios where any permitted bus measurement device fails. On the IEEE 15 bus feeder, this paper compares TANFL with a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) and the formula-based localization method under identical data, measurement availability scenarios, and evaluation metrics. On the test partition, TANFL outperforms the conventional MLP; with complete measurements, its line fault location performance is slightly lower than that of the formula-based method, but in the average results for scenarios with one missing bus measurement block, its accuracy is the highest among the three methods at a 5% tolerance.

authors.name: Xingpeng Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Log-concavity of longest increasing subsequence
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture proposed by Chen that, for every fixed $n$, the sequence $(a_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave, where $a_{n,k}$ counts permutations of $[n]$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$.

authors.name: Yupeng Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: ETC-Bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluation-Side Transcript Canonicalization
papers.abstract: Written transcripts of the same speech can differ in ways that are not uniquely determined by the speech signal. We formulate evaluation-side transcript canonicalization (ETC), which maps multiple surface forms to a single canonical form when their differences are not determined by speech. To our knowledge, ETC-Bench is the first and most comprehensive multilingual benchmark for evaluation-side transcript canonicalization, covering 181 phenomenon types across 12 languages. Each instance is a minimal pair that shares a sentence context and differs only in a target span exhibiting one phenomenon. To evaluate both canonicalization success and semantic preservation, we propose Semantic-preserving Exact-match Normalization Accuracy (SENA), which combines exact agreement between independently canonicalized pair members with a pair-relative BERTScore constraint against information loss. We further introduce the Taxonomy-guided Agent Canonicalization Skill (TACS), which provides LLM agents with phenomenon descriptions and explicit canonicalization contracts. Experiments with five baseline configurations and three TACS-based agents show that the agents outperform the baseline systems on shared languages. ETC-Bench provides a systematic testbed for evaluation-side transcript canonicalization across languages.

authors.name: Junhao Du
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: A Trainable CPG Framework for Quadruped Locomotion
papers.abstract: We present CPG-ENN, a trainable quadruped locomotion framework that combines explicit neural coordination with learned motion realization. A symmetry-based eight-neuron central pattern generator (CPG) supplies gait rhythms, while a pretrained, leg-shared execution neural network (ENN) maps rhythmic signals and trajectory parameters to joint-angle references without online inverse kinematics. A single feedback policy modulates six physically interpretable trajectory variables. The controller tracks planar velocity and yaw-rate commands across walk, trot, pace, bound, and pronk without gait-specific learned controllers or transitionspecific rewards. Simulation yields 99.39% transition success across all 20 directed gait pairs and all source-target speed combinations from {0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0} m/s. Ablations show high cross-gait transition feasibility without transition exposure; exposure mainly refines gait acquisition and velocity transients. Comparisons with AllGaits and Walk These Ways demonstrate accurate gait-speed regulation, and Unitree Go2 experiments validate five gaits and their transitions.

authors.name: Yide Liu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Guoyong Mao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems

authors.name: Shaoxing Qu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems

papers.title: Learning from Points and Patches: A Pre-trained Hybrid Attention Transformer for Time Series Analysis
papers.abstract:
Time-series data generated by Web services and connected systems support applications such as user activity analysis, service monitoring, and resource management. However, learning transferable representations from heterogeneous time series remains challenging due to diverse temporal patterns, variable sequence lengths, and limited high-quality annotations. Despite the success of pre-training in natural language processing and computer vision, effective time-series pre-training requires strategies tailored to temporal data.
  We propose TimeHAT (Hybrid Attention Transformer), a general-purpose pre-training framework for time-series analysis that addresses two complementary questions: what to learn and how to learn. For what to learn, we introduce a Unified Point-Patch Masking Strategy (UPPMS) that integrates point-level and patch-level supervision within a unified framework for contextual reconstruction and causal extrapolation, enabling the model to capture both fine-grained temporal variations and broader temporal patterns. For how to learn, we develop a Hybrid Attention Encoder (HAE) that combines prefix-constrained bidirectional attention in initial layers with directional hybrid attention in deeper layers, aiming to preserve effective contextual interactions while mitigating rank degeneration.
  We evaluate TimeHAT across real-world datasets and four downstream tasks: classification, long-term forecasting, imputation, and anomaly detection. Experiments cover fine-tuning, few-shot, and zero-shot transfer settings, demonstrating competitive performance across diverse time-series analysis tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/TangPeiwang/TimeHAT.

authors.name: Peiwang Tang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Weitai Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Less is more: learning what to profile for GPU kernel optimization
papers.abstract: Large language models have recently shown strong potential for automatically optimizing GPU kernels, yet their effectiveness depends critically on the hardware information available to the kernel optimization model. Existing systems typically rely on predefined profiling strategies, leaving what to profile largely outside the optimization process. We show that effective profiling is not simply about collecting more information: increasing the number of profiling metrics does not monotonically improve kernel optimization, while the most useful profiling information varies across kernels. Our theoretical analysis further shows that, under such heterogeneous profiling utility, kernel-conditioned selection can outperform any single fixed profiling configuration. Motivated by this observation, we propose AutoProfiler, a feedback-driven framework for learning a deterministic profiling tree from optimization feedback. The tree is iteratively refined through REWRITE and SPLIT operations, with an LLM generating candidate modifications and empirical evaluation determining their acceptance. Once constructed, the tree quickly gathers the required profiling information for any kernel, allowing the LLM rewriter to be invoked only once. Experiments on KernelBench show that our approach improves kernel optimization over fixed profiling configurations under constrained profiling budgets. These results suggest that hardware profiling should evolve from static metric collection toward profiling reasoning, making profiling itself a new dimension for improving kernel optimization. The codes are available at https://github.com/Satissss/AutoProfiler.

authors.name: Runyu Chen
authors.institution: University of International Business and Economics

papers.title: Ferron-driven motion of non-collinear ferroelectric domain walls
papers.abstract: We study the propagation of ferrons, the quanta of electric polarization waves, through a ferroelectric texture. We predict by analytic and numerical calculations that a $90^\circ$ domain wall (DW) operates as a beam splitter of longitudinal ferron and transverse optical phonon modes. An associated momentum-flux imbalance leads to forces that drive DW motion. In the weak-anisotropy limit, the DW becomes a rotating texture with nearly fixed-modulus, whose low-energy dynamics is described by a sine-Gordon equation. A ferron source then attracts the DW through a damping-induced force. Both driving forces scale linearly with incident wave intensity. Our results uncover qualitatively different routes to driven ferroelectric DW motion enabled by the vector nature of the polarization and offer functionalities for THz ferroelectric devices.

papers.title: Revisiting the Photometric Modulation Amplitudes of Kepler Planet Hosts: A Confounder-Adjusted Test of Stellar Spin-Orbit Alignment
papers.abstract: T. Mazeh and coworkers pioneered a method using rotational photometric modulation as a proxy to infer stellar obliquities in Kepler transiting planetary systems, based on the expected positive correlation between spot-induced modulation amplitudes and stellar inclinations. They found that planet hosts cooler than the Sun showed larger modulation amplitudes than comparison stars, consistent with low stellar obliquities. For hotter hosts, however, they reported the opposite - a negative amplitude difference (hosts minus comparison stars) - which is difficult to interpret in terms of viewing geometry. We show that this comparison is affected by confounding variables not controlled for in the sample selection. One such confounder is apparent magnitude, whose distributions differ markedly between the two samples for hotter stars and affect the observed modulation amplitudes. We develop resampling and likelihood-based approaches that enable comparison of the amplitude distributions at fixed apparent magnitude, stellar radius, and rotation period. The previously reported negative amplitude difference for hot hosts is no longer present in either analysis. The likelihood-based analysis finds a positive amplitude difference up to $\sim 6100\,\mathrm{K}$ that becomes consistent with zero at higher temperatures, while the resampling analysis shows a similar but less pronounced trend. This result is qualitatively consistent with independent $v\sin i$ analyses suggesting low obliquities for cooler super-Earth and sub-Neptune hosts and broader obliquity distributions for hotter ones. This may also indicate a gradual change in the obliquity distribution with stellar temperature, although changes in spot distributions or selection effects could also contribute to the photometric trends in hot stars.

papers.title: RoboSTD: Zero-Shot Single-to-Dual Transfer via Sagittal Mirroring for Bimanual Learning
papers.abstract: Bimanual robot manipulation plays an important role in real-world robotic applications, but the high cost of collecting bimanual demonstrations limits the scalable development of bimanual policy learning. Meanwhile, existing single-arm manipulation data are difficult to directly transfer to bimanual systems due to the Single-to-Dual gap in action spaces, coordination requirements, and arm-side spatial preference. To address this issue, we propose RoboSTD, a zero-shot Single-to-Dual data construction method for bimanual robot learning. RoboSTD first applies sagittal-plane mirroring to observations, proprioception, and actions to construct executable contralateral pseudo-demonstrations. It then uses an LLM to generate structured spatio-temporal coordination constraints that guide the reconstruction of pseudo-bimanual supervision across workspace regions and task stages. We evaluate RoboSTD on the AgileX ALOHA platform in both RoboTwin simulation and real-world settings. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RoboSTD for bimanual policy learning. Without requiring additional bimanual demonstrations, RoboSTD increases the average number of collected cups to 2.11x that of the single-arm baseline in the cup collection task. Project page: https://huahungy.github.io/RoboSTD/

authors.name: Hongyu Wu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: The Exact Weight Spectrum of $\RM(m-7,m$): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Sol\'{e} Conjecture
papers.abstract: Boolean functions are widely used in cryptography and coding theory. A key challenge lies in finding the weight spectrum for all $n$-variable Boolean functions of degree at most $r$, also known as the Reed--Muller code $\RM(r,n)$. In 2023, Carlet and Sol\'{e} determined the weight spectra of $\RM(n-c,n)$ for $c=3,4$, and conjectured the weight spectrum of $\RM(n-c, n$) for $n\ge2c$. The weight spectra of $\RM(n-5, n)$ and $\RM(n-6,n)$ were determined by Carlet in 2024 and by Lou and Wang in 2025, respectively, confirming the Carlet-Sol\'{e} conjecture for the cases $c=5,6$. Very recently, Leuenberger et al. and Wei et al. investigated the weight spectrum of $\RM(7,14)$ independently, and there are eight potential weights which have not been determined. Up until now, the weight spectra of the Reed--Muller codes $RM(r,n)$ are still unknown for $r=3,...,n-7$. In this paper, we determine the exact weight spectrum of $\RM(m-7, m)$ for every $m\ge 14$. By combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, we exclude the conjectured eight weights for $\RM(7,14)$. We then extend the exclusions to all higher dimensions using a geometric transfer. Consequently, we provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Sol\'{e} conjecture.

papers.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
papers.abstract: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

papers.title: RankFormer: Rethinking Time Series Transformers through Representation Capacity Analysis and Progressive Decoding
papers.abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a critical role in Web and cyber-physical systems, where large-scale services and IoT infrastructures generate complex temporal data. Transformer-based models have achieved strong empirical performance in this domain, yet the principles governing the expressive capacity of their learned representations remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, many existing models rely on simplified decoding strategies, including channel-independent modeling and direct projection heads, which limit their ability to capture complex multivariate dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose RankFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for multivariate time series forecasting. We establish a rank-based analysis framework to investigate how tokenization, embedding, and attention designs affect the representation capacity of time series Transformers. Our analysis reveals that patchification increases the potential representation capacity by aggregating multiple temporal observations into each token, while subsequent encoding operations determine how much of this capacity is realized. Guided by these insights, we develop a rank-enhancing encoder with Hourglass Attention to improve rank stability during information interaction. Furthermore, we introduce the Interactive Progressive Decoder (IPD), which improves future trajectory modeling through global-guided cross-channel interaction and progressive refinement. Extensive experiments on real-world long-term forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that RankFormer achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods. Code repository: https://github.com/TangPeiwang/Rankformer.

authors.name: Peiwang Tang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Development of a real-time FPGA-based CNN trigger operating on full-granularity calorimeter images
papers.abstract: We present a real-time field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for event classification on full calorimeter images that retain crystal-level shower information. To meet the resource and latency constraints of trigger electronics, the network parameters and hidden activations were quantized to 8 bits with quantization-aware training, and a lossless space-to-depth reorganization rearranged the input image into fewer spatial positions, reducing the estimated CNN inference latency by more than an order of magnitude. The approach was evaluated with the J-PARC KOTO detector, recorded data, and data-acquisition (DAQ) constraints as a benchmark, targeting the online separation of the rare $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ decay from its dominant $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ background. As a proof of principle, the firmware was implemented and validated on an AMD Versal Premium VPK120 evaluation board. On 100,000 test events, inference on the board rejected $(99.34\pm0.04)\%$ of the recorded background sample enriched in $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ decays at a nominal $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ efficiency of 95%, with a measured CNN inference latency of 17.9 $\mu$s. Combining the measured image-assembly and CNN inference latencies with the estimated link-transfer and score-return times gives a projected end-to-end latency of 25.9 $\mu$s, within the adopted 32 $\mu$s DAQ latency budget. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using full-granularity calorimeter images for CNN-based event selection that achieves high background rejection while keeping the trigger latency within tens of microseconds.

papers.title: Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.

papers.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
papers.abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.

authors.name: Li Zhu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. Our model, interpolative FLow EXpert (iFLEX), first estimates the missing field by taking a weighted average of the two observations at each grid point, giving more weight to the observation closer to the requested time. During training, subtracting this estimate from an observed intermediate field gives the residual that a conditional diffusion model learns to generate. Both observations condition the model, together with the target time, the interval between observations, and available physical parameters. To reconstruct an unobserved intermediate field, the generated residual is added to the weighted average. We evaluate iFLEX on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature. Across these datasets, iFLEX achieves lower reconstruction error than the evaluated baselines, including optical-flow and diffusion models developed for video frame interpolation in computer vision. In a controlled turbulence comparison at a Reynolds number of 36,000, learning the residual reduces relative Frobenius norm error from about 13.7 for direct field generation to 10.5, with the diffusion backbone and training setup held fixed. Code is available at https://github.com/paulpuren/iflex.

papers.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution
papers.abstract: Gradient-based data attribution has become an important tool for high-quality data selection in the instruction fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), as it estimates the contribution of training examples through their influence on model optimization. However, we find that existing global gradient attribution methods suffer from surface-form bias: minor changes to semantically irrelevant details, such as wording or formatting, can produce highly inconsistent attribution scores even when the underlying content remains unchanged. To address this issue, we propose Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution (CIGA), a robust framework for instruction data selection. CIGA first identifies layers whose gradients are both influential for attribution and stable under semantics-preserving surface-form perturbations, thereby reducing formatting noise in gradient features. It then dynamically fuses these attribution signals with semantic representations of the input, combining optimization-level influence with content-level information. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that CIGA produces more stable rankings under surface-form perturbations while preserving downstream capabilities and improving average performance. CIGA also reduces attribution cost, offering a robust and efficient approach to data selection for LLM instruction tuning.

papers.title: Language Models Keep Abandoned Analyses: Residue and Adaptation after Garden-Path Sentences
papers.abstract: Reading "While the man hunted the deer ran into the woods" requires giving up the analysis in which "the deer" is the object of "hunted". People who have just read such a sentence still produce more transitive structures, so the abandoned analysis primes later language. We ask whether language models keep using an analysis they have abandoned, and what in the model carries it. In 24 open models from 124M to 70B parameters, a garden-path sentence leaves two traces in the context. A residue of the abandoned analysis raises later object attachment, by about three quarters of the effect of a sentence in which the noun phrase really is an object, and it appears in sampled text, on held-out and human-normed items and for a second type of garden path. An adaptation toward the resolved structure scales with the sentence's disambiguation error and acts mainly on comprehension-like measures. Activation patching separates the two. Later text reads the residue from the role information in the noun phrase's states, which were computed under the object analysis before the disambiguation, and replacing these states removes almost all of the residue in the 32B and 70B models. The adaptation is read from the states that processed the disambiguation. Overridden statements show the same persistence (a corrected value keeps pulling later predictions in 8 of 9 models), and in most models the pull is carried by the positions after the statement. Finally, the human paradigm transfers only with controls for punctuation, because the models also write garden-path sentences themselves, which reverses the paradigm's raw statistic.

papers.title: Weakness Localization Is Not Enough: State-Aware Recursive Knowledge Improvement for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Knowledge improvement in large language models is shifting from predefined knowledge incorporation pipelines toward evaluation-guided updating. Existing methods use evaluation to localize model-specific knowledge weaknesses and guide targeted post-training. However, identifying what to improve does not necessarily provide sufficient information for deciding how to improve it. The same localized weakness can be compatible with distinct operational knowledge states: the relevant knowledge may be unavailable, available but difficult to access reliably, or accessible but ineffective for downstream use. We call this ambiguity knowledge-state aliasing. When compatible states favor different interventions, greater diagnostic resolution alone is insufficient for intervention selection. Moreover, model updates can change the underlying knowledge state before the observed weakness disappears, such that an intervention appropriate in one round may no longer address the bottleneck in the next. To address these challenges, we propose Recursive Knowledge Improvement (RKI), which formulates knowledge improvement as a sequential, state-aware intervention process. RKI organizes knowledge into graph-structured units that provide a shared basis for diagnostic evaluation and targeted intervention across rounds. At each round, RKI localizes knowledge weaknesses, estimates the model's operational knowledge state from diagnostic evidence and intervention history, selects a corresponding intervention, and re-evaluates the updated model before determining the next intervention. On HotpotEval and SafeInternalEval, RKI outperforms existing knowledge incorporation methods by 18.41 points on average. Further analyses show that knowledge states provide additional guidance for intervention selection beyond weakness localization and can change across model updates even when the observed weakness persists.

authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Bingyu Zhu
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

papers.title: Words or Deeds? How LLMs Predict Users' Decisions in Human-Agent Dialogue
papers.abstract: Web systems increasingly predict users' decisions from what users say, yet when interests partly conflict, users may promise to cooperate to win the other side's cooperation and then not do so. Sales or service agents that rely on such promises may grant concessions to users who then do not keep their promises, at a cost to the party they represent. We test how LLMs combine users' statements with decision records to predict users' decisions, using 1,260 rounds in which 42 users played a repeated prisoner's dilemma-style game with five agents, each prompted to express a dominant Big Five trait, and could talk with the agent before every decision. Across eight open-weight LLMs, predictions from decision records separated cooperation from defection well (AUC = .80), and adding dialogue brought no detectable gain. With dialogue, predictions agreed with users' statements more often, and errors concentrated on rounds in which users broke their statements: accuracy on rounds with a statement barely changed (.73 to .74), while it rose on kept statements (.76 to .95) and fell sharply on broken ones (.65 to .17). Predictions weighted statements more heavily than users' behavior warranted: when users stated a decision they had not yet made in that game, the predicted probability of keeping it rose from .13 to .69, whereas users kept .40 of such statements. Users' decisions also varied with the agent they faced, but predictions hardly reflected this: users cooperated more with the Agreeableness agent than with the Extraversion agent (70.6% vs. 54.5%), whereas predicted cooperation was nearly identical (64.5% vs. 63.1%). Users also cooperated more with an agent when they themselves scored higher on that agent's trait, whereas predicted cooperation barely changed with these scores. Dialogue-based predictions should therefore weigh users' statements by their earlier decisions and the agent they face.

authors.name: Yuying Tang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Yong-Jin Liu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Who Knows What - and What Does It Support? Perspective-Bounded Evidence Calibration for Multimodal Theory of Mind
papers.abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer others' beliefs, goals, and intentions, is a cornerstone of social intelligence. Multimodal ToM requires inferring an agent's mental state from evidence that is available to that agent, rather than from the complete episode observed by the solver. Existing LLM-based and Bayesian model-based approaches reconstruct global event traces, yet they do not explicitly distinguish objective events from agent-admissible evidence during hypothesis evaluation. Consequently, agent-inaccessible events or semantically misaligned actions and utterances may influence the inferred belief, goal, or social intention, leading to perspective leakage and source or route confusion. We formulate this limitation as an evidence-admissibility problem: evidence should contribute to a mental-state hypothesis only when it is accessible to the relevant agent, preserves its information source, and is diagnostic of the queried mental-state variable. To operationalize this principle, we propose PIP-ToM, an evidence-admissibility interface that constructs agent-specific evidence stores, aligns them with structured mental-state claims, and calibrates model-based hypothesis scores while preserving the underlying Bayesian inference process. PIP-ToM with GPT-4o outperforms existing ToM methods across MuMA-ToM, MMToM-QA, and Hi-ToM, achieving average accuracies of 92.56%, 95.00%, and 95.00%, respectively.

authors.name: Kedi Lyu
authors.institution: Jilin Province Science and Technology Department

papers.title: Kinetic Sectors and Nonequilibrium Dynamics in the $\delta$-Ising Model
papers.abstract: We introduce and analyze the $\delta$-Ising model, a kinetic Ising ferromagnet in which single-spin flips are accepted when their energy change does not exceed a tunable threshold. Varying the field and threshold opens or closes local flip channels, dividing parameter space into kinetic sectors, each governed by a fixed Markov transition operator. We prove that the dynamics retains global spin-inversion symmetry exactly when up and down spins have equal numbers of open channels. In one such sector on a periodic chain of length $L$, unbiased random initial states therefore reach the field-aligned and antifield states with probability $1/2$ each. Closing a single channel leaves both states absorbing but makes the probability of ordering against the field decay as $(2/\pi)^L$. Parameter sweeps correspond to ordered products of sector operators, which separate reaching a state from holding it, so hysteresis appears when a state is reached and released at different sector boundaries. We also show how increasing the system size can induce a Mpemba-like reversal, allowing a state with more misaligned spins to reach the final ordered state sooner on average. On a periodic chain, this reversal arises because the mean absorption time grows logarithmically with system size for many short domains but linearly for a single macroscopic domain, and it disappears when the bulk flip channel is opened. These findings show how a simple, intuitive rule for Ising dynamics links local kinetic constraints to field response, memory, and relaxation within a unified framework.

authors.name: Dehen Cao
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Wei Jiang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology
